english: to have one thing replaced with another, to change
note: 'Berganti' means something changes or is replaced (e.g. clothes, seasons, shifts); related to 'ganti' (replace/change), often used in everyday contexts like changing clothes or shifts.

sentences.text: Dia berganti baju sebelum pergi ke sekolah.
sentences.en: She changes her clothes before going to school.

sentences.text: Musim hujan berganti menjadi musim panas.
sentences.en: The rainy season changes into the dry season.

sentences.text: Ayah berganti sepatu di depan rumah.
sentences.en: Dad changes his shoes in front of the house.

english: to change, to evolve, to be different from before
note: "Berubah" is a common everyday verb meaning something has changed state; often confused with "mengubah" (to actively change something); related words: "perubahan" (change/noun), "berubah-ubah" (keeps changing).

sentences.text: Cuaca di Bali sering berubah.
sentences.en: The weather in Bali often changes.

sentences.text: Harga makanan itu sudah berubah.
sentences.en: The price of that food has already changed.

sentences.text: Dia berubah setelah tinggal di sini.
sentences.en: She changed after living here.

note: 'Kata kerja' literally means 'action word' and is the standard term for verb in Indonesian grammar; beginners often confuse it with 'kata benda' (noun) or 'kata sifat' (adjective).

sentences.text: 'Makan' adalah kata kerja dalam bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: 'Makan' (eat) is a verb in the Indonesian language.

sentences.text: Guru menjelaskan apa itu kata kerja.
sentences.en: The teacher explains what a verb is.

sentences.text: Saya belajar kata kerja baru hari ini.
sentences.en: I learned a new verb today.

note: Informal/neutral verb; 'pukul' is the root, 'memukul' is the active form; also note 'pukul' separately means 'o'clock' (e.g., pukul tiga = 3 o'clock).

sentences.text: Anak itu memukul bola dengan keras.
sentences.en: That child hits the ball hard.

sentences.text: Jangan memukul temanmu di sekolah.
sentences.en: Don't hit your friend at school.

sentences.text: Dia memukul meja karena marah.
sentences.en: He hit the table because he was angry.

english: to receive something, to accept something
note: "Menerima" is the formal/active form; "terima" appears in common phrases like "terima kasih" (thank you); often confused with "mendapat" (to get/receive by chance).

sentences.text: Saya menerima hadiah dari teman saya.
sentences.en: I receive a gift from my friend.

sentences.text: Dia menerima telepon di kamar.
sentences.en: She accepts a phone call in the room.

sentences.text: Kami menerima tamu di rumah.
sentences.en: We receive guests at home.

english: to take/accompany someone somewhere, to deliver something or someone to a certain place
note: "Mengantar" is the formal/written form; in casual speech Indonesians often drop the prefix and say "antar" — it means to take or accompany someone to a place, not just to go yourself.

sentences.text: Ayah mengantar saya ke sekolah setiap pagi.
sentences.en: Dad takes me to school every morning.

sentences.text: Saya mengantar teman ke bandara kemarin.
sentences.en: I took my friend to the airport yesterday.

sentences.text: Bisakah kamu antar saya ke pasar?
sentences.en: Can you take me to the market?

english: to arrange something, to regulate something
note: 'Mengatur' is the formal/written form; 'atur' is the root used in casual speech; related words include 'peraturan' (rule/regulation) and 'teratur' (orderly).

sentences.text: Ibu mengatur meja makan setiap hari.
sentences.en: Mom arranges the dining table every day.

sentences.text: Pak guru mengatur jadwal kelas kami.
sentences.en: The teacher regulates our class schedule.

sentences.text: Dia mengatur barang-barang di kamar.
sentences.en: She arranges the items in the room.

note: 'Menggoreng' is the formal/active form; everyday speech often shortens to 'goreng' (e.g., 'goreng telur'); commonly confused with 'memasak' (to cook in general).

sentences.text: Ibu menggoreng ayam di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is frying chicken in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Saya suka goreng tempe setiap pagi.
sentences.en: I like to fry tempeh every morning.

sentences.text: Dia menggoreng telur untuk sarapan.
sentences.en: He is frying an egg for breakfast.

note: "Menghitung" is the formal/full form; "hitung" is the root used in commands or compounds (e.g., "hitung dulu" = count first); do not confuse with "menghitung" (to calculate) vs. "membayar" (to pay).

sentences.text: Ayo hitung jumlah mangga di keranjang.
sentences.en: Let's count the number of mangoes in the basket.

sentences.text: Ibu menghitung uang di dompetnya.
sentences.en: Mom is counting the money in her wallet.

sentences.text: Tolong hitung murid di kelas ini.
sentences.en: Please count the students in this class.

note: 'Mengirim' is the formal/full form; 'kirim' is the informal root often used in casual speech; commonly used for sending messages, packages, or money.

sentences.text: Saya mengirim pesan kepada teman saya.
sentences.en: I send a message to my friend.

sentences.text: Ibu kirim uang ke adik setiap bulan.
sentences.en: Mom sends money to my younger sibling every month.

sentences.text: Kami mengirim paket ke Bali hari ini.
sentences.en: We send a package to Bali today.

note: "Mengisi" is the active verb form; "isi" is the root meaning 'content/fill'; commonly used for filling forms, bottles, or fuel.

sentences.text: Tolong mengisi botol ini dengan air.
sentences.en: Please fill this bottle with water.

sentences.text: Saya harus mengisi formulir itu sekarang.
sentences.en: I have to fill out that form now.

sentences.text: Dia mengisi bensin di pom bensin.
sentences.en: He fills up fuel at the gas station.

note: 'Nikah' is the base form (formal/Islamic context); 'menikah' is the active verb meaning 'to get married'; related: 'pernikahan' (wedding/marriage), 'suami' (husband), 'istri' (wife).

sentences.text: Kakak saya akan menikah bulan depan.
sentences.en: My older sibling will get married next month.

sentences.text: Mereka menikah di Bali tahun lalu.
sentences.en: They got married in Bali last year.

sentences.text: Kapan kamu mau nikah?
sentences.en: When do you want to get married?

english: to shut something, to close something
note: "Tutup" is the root; "menutup" is the active verb form (me- prefix); also means 'closed' as an adjective (e.g. toko tutup = the shop is closed); don't confuse with "menutup" (to cover) vs "mengunci" (to lock).

sentences.text: Tolong tutup pintu itu sekarang.
sentences.en: Please close that door now.

sentences.text: Dia menutup jendela karena hujan.
sentences.en: She closes the window because of rain.

sentences.text: Anak itu menutup bukunya dengan cepat.
sentences.en: The child closes his book quickly.

english: to store something away, to save/deposit money
note: "Menyimpan" is the active verb form; use "simpan" for commands (e.g., 'Simpan ini!'); often confused with "menabung" which specifically means saving money in a bank.

sentences.text: Saya menyimpan uang di bank setiap minggu.
sentences.en: I save money at the bank every week.

sentences.text: Ibu menyimpan baju bersih di lemari.
sentences.en: Mom stores the clean clothes in the wardrobe.

sentences.text: Tolong simpan makanan ini di kulkas.
sentences.en: Please store this food in the fridge.

english: to feel (an emotion), to feel that...
note: "Merasa" means to feel an emotion or sense something; often confused with "merasakan" (to experience/taste); "rasa" alone can mean feeling or taste.

sentences.text: Saya merasa senang hari ini.
sentences.en: I feel happy today.

sentences.text: Dia merasa lelah setelah bekerja.
sentences.en: She feels tired after working.

sentences.text: Kami merasa lapar sekarang.
sentences.en: We feel hungry now.

note: 'Mohon' is a formal/polite way to request something, stronger than 'minta'; often seen in signs, announcements, and respectful speech.

sentences.text: Mohon tunggu sebentar, ya.
sentences.en: Please wait a moment, okay.

sentences.text: Saya mohon bantuan dari kamu.
sentences.en: I respectfully ask for your help.

sentences.text: Mohon maaf, saya terlambat hari ini.
sentences.en: I sincerely apologize, I am late today.

note: 'Pena' means pen (writing instrument); not to be confused with 'pensil' (pencil); commonly used in school and office contexts.

sentences.text: Saya butuh pena untuk menulis surat.
sentences.en: I need a pen to write a letter.

sentences.text: Boleh saya pinjam pena kamu?
sentences.en: May I borrow your pen?

sentences.text: Pena saya ada di dalam tas.
sentences.en: My pen is inside the bag.

note: 'Pensil' is an everyday neutral word for pencil; borrowed from Dutch 'penseel'; often paired with 'buku' (book) or 'kertas' (paper) in school contexts.

sentences.text: Saya punya satu pensil di tas.
sentences.en: I have one pencil in my bag.

sentences.text: Tolong berikan pensil itu kepada saya.
sentences.en: Please give that pencil to me.

sentences.text: Pensil saya hilang di sekolah.
sentences.en: My pencil got lost at school.

english: a feeling, a sense, a sensation of something
note: "Rasa" means feeling, taste, or sensation; also used in "rasanya" (it feels like); don't confuse with "merasa" (to feel as a verb).

sentences.text: Saya punya rasa senang hari ini.
sentences.en: I have a feeling of happiness today.

sentences.text: Ada rasa dingin di pantai ini.
sentences.en: There is a cold sensation at this beach.

sentences.text: Rasa makanan ini sangat enak.
sentences.en: The taste of this food is very delicious.

note: 'Sedih' is a common, neutral word for sadness; related words include 'kesedihan' (sadness/noun) and 'menyedihkan' (sad/pitiful as adjective).

sentences.text: Dia sedih karena kehilangan kucing kesayangannya.
sentences.en: She is sad because she lost her beloved cat.

sentences.text: Saya merasa sedih hari ini.
sentences.en: I feel sad today.

sentences.text: Anak itu menangis karena sangat sedih.
sentences.en: The child is crying because they are very sad.

note: 'Kamus' means dictionary; it is a noun used the same for singular and plural; commonly paired with 'kamus bahasa Inggris' (English dictionary).

sentences.text: Saya punya kamus bahasa Inggris di rumah.
sentences.en: I have an English dictionary at home.

sentences.text: Tolong bawa kamus ke kelas besok.
sentences.en: Please bring a dictionary to class tomorrow.

sentences.text: Dia mencari kata di kamus itu.
sentences.en: He is looking up a word in that dictionary.

english: to cut something, to cut something off
note: Use 'memotong' in formal/written contexts and 'potong' in everyday speech; also means 'to cut' hair, paper, or food; related: 'gunting' (scissors).

sentences.text: Ibu memotong sayuran di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is cutting vegetables in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Ayah potong rambut saya hari ini.
sentences.en: Dad cuts my hair today.

sentences.text: Tolong potong kue itu untuk kami.
sentences.en: Please cut that cake for us.

english: to plant something, to grow something e.g. a crop
note: "Menanam" is the active verb form (me- prefix on root "tanam"); used for planting crops, seeds, or trees; beginners sometimes confuse it with "tumbuh" (to grow/sprout, intransitive).

sentences.text: Ibu menanam sayuran di kebun.
sentences.en: Mother plants vegetables in the garden.

sentences.text: Kami menanam padi setiap tahun.
sentences.en: We grow rice every year.

sentences.text: Ayah menanam pohon di depan rumah.
sentences.en: Father plants a tree in front of the house.

note: 'Mengubah' is the formal/active form; 'ubah' is the root — use 'mengubah' in everyday sentences; not to be confused with 'mengganti' (to replace/swap).

sentences.text: Dia ingin mengubah warna rambutnya.
sentences.en: She wants to change her hair color.

sentences.text: Tolong ubah jadwal kita besok.
sentences.en: Please change our schedule for tomorrow.

sentences.text: Saya mengubah resep masakan ini.
sentences.en: I am changing this cooking recipe.

english: rice (as it grows in a paddy field or dry field), a rice plant
note: 'Padi' refers to the rice plant or unhusked rice in the field; 'beras' is uncooked milled rice and 'nasi' is cooked rice — a common source of confusion for beginners.

sentences.text: Petani menanam padi di sawah.
sentences.en: The farmer plants rice in the paddy field.

sentences.text: Padi itu sudah tumbuh tinggi.
sentences.en: The rice plant has already grown tall.

sentences.text: Kami melihat padi di ladang.
sentences.en: We see rice plants in the field.

note: "Akuntan" is a formal/neutral noun for accountant; related words include "akuntansi" (accounting) and "keuangan" (finance).

sentences.text: Ayah saya bekerja sebagai akuntan.
sentences.en: My father works as an accountant.

sentences.text: Dia adalah akuntan di kantor besar.
sentences.en: She is an accountant at a big office.

sentences.text: Saya ingin menjadi akuntan profesional.
sentences.en: I want to become a professional accountant.

note: "Dokter gigi" literally means "tooth doctor"; use it with "ke" (to go to) or "adalah" (is); related: "dokter" (doctor), "gigi" (tooth/teeth).

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke dokter gigi hari ini.
sentences.en: I am going to the dentist today.

sentences.text: Dokter gigi itu sangat baik.
sentences.en: That dentist is very kind.

sentences.text: Ibu membawa adik ke dokter gigi.
sentences.en: Mom takes my younger sibling to the dentist.

note: 'Efisien' is a neutral/formal loanword from English; often paired with 'kerja' (work) or 'cara' (method); synonym 'hemat' focuses more on saving resources.

sentences.text: Cara ini sangat efisien untuk memasak nasi.
sentences.en: This way is very efficient for cooking rice.

sentences.text: Pak Made bekerja dengan cara yang efisien.
sentences.en: Mr. Made works in an efficient way.

sentences.text: Motor lebih efisien daripada mobil di Bali.
sentences.en: Motorcycles are more efficient than cars in Bali.

note: 'Gagal' means to fail or not succeed; often used with 'ujian' (exam) or plans; related: 'berhasil' (to succeed) is its opposite.

sentences.text: Dia gagal ujian matematika kemarin.
sentences.en: He failed the math exam yesterday.

sentences.text: Saya tidak mau gagal lagi.
sentences.en: I don't want to fail again.

sentences.text: Rencana kami gagal karena hujan.
sentences.en: Our plan failed because of rain.

note: 'Ibu rumah tangga' is a neutral, everyday term for housewife; often shortened to 'IRT' in writing; related: 'ibu' (mother/woman), 'rumah tangga' (household).

sentences.text: Ibu saya adalah seorang ibu rumah tangga.
sentences.en: My mother is a housewife.

sentences.text: Dia bekerja sebagai ibu rumah tangga di rumah.
sentences.en: She works as a housewife at home.

note: 'Insinyur' is a formal/common noun for engineer, often abbreviated as 'Ir.' before a name; used in everyday speech without articles.

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang insinyur.
sentences.en: My father is an engineer.

sentences.text: Dia bekerja sebagai insinyur di Bali.
sentences.en: He works as an engineer in Bali.

sentences.text: Saya ingin menjadi insinyur.
sentences.en: I want to become an engineer.

english: a type, a category, a class of something, a species of something
note: "Jenis" is neutral and everyday; often used like "type" or "kind", e.g. "jenis makanan" (type of food); related: "macam" (kind/sort), "tipe" (type, borrowed).

sentences.text: Ada banyak jenis buah di pasar.
sentences.en: There are many types of fruit at the market.

sentences.text: Apa jenis musik yang kamu suka?
sentences.en: What type of music do you like?

sentences.text: Ini jenis anjing yang sangat lucu.
sentences.en: This is a type of dog that is very cute.

note: 'Marah' means angry; say 'marah-marah' to mean scolding/ranting; related: 'kesal' (annoyed), 'jengkel' (irritated); used in everyday informal speech.

sentences.text: Ibu marah karena saya pulang terlambat.
sentences.en: Mom is angry because I came home late.

sentences.text: Jangan marah, ini hanya kesalahan kecil.
sentences.en: Don't be angry, this is just a small mistake.

sentences.text: Dia marah kepada temannya hari ini.
sentences.en: He is angry at his friend today.

note: "Mengetik" is the formal verb form; "ketik" is the root used in casual speech and commands (e.g., "ketik di sini" = "type here"); often used for typing on phones or computers.

sentences.text: Saya mengetik pesan untuk teman saya.
sentences.en: I am typing a message for my friend.

sentences.text: Dia mengetik dengan cepat di komputer.
sentences.en: She types quickly on the computer.

sentences.text: Tolong ketik nama kamu di sini.
sentences.en: Please type your name here.

note: "Montir" is an informal/colloquial word for mechanic, commonly used in everyday speech; the more formal term is "mekanik".

sentences.text: Montir itu sedang memperbaiki motor saya.
sentences.en: The mechanic is fixing my motorbike.

sentences.text: Ayah saya bekerja sebagai montir.
sentences.en: My father works as a mechanic.

sentences.text: Saya perlu mencari montir yang bagus.
sentences.en: I need to find a good mechanic.

note: 'Pegawai negeri' means a government/civil servant; also called 'PNS' (Pegawai Negeri Sipil) in everyday speech; not to be confused with 'karyawan' (private employee).

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah pegawai negeri di kantor.
sentences.en: My father is a civil servant at the office.

sentences.text: Ibu ingin menjadi pegawai negeri.
sentences.en: Mom wants to become a civil servant.

sentences.text: Pegawai negeri bekerja untuk pemerintah.
sentences.en: A civil servant works for the government.

note: 'Pelayan' means waiter/waitress in a restaurant; root word 'layan' relates to serving, and 'melayani' means 'to serve'.

sentences.text: Pelayan itu membawa makanan ke meja kami.
sentences.en: The waiter brought food to our table.

sentences.text: Saya memanggil pelayan untuk memesan minuman.
sentences.en: I called the waitress to order a drink.

sentences.text: Pelayan di restoran ini sangat ramah.
sentences.en: The waiter at this restaurant is very friendly.

note: 'Pemain' means player or actor; it comes from the root word 'main' (to play); also used in sports and games contexts.

sentences.text: Dia adalah pemain sepak bola yang bagus.
sentences.en: He is a good soccer player.

sentences.text: Pemain itu bermain di lapangan besar.
sentences.en: The player plays on a big field.

english: a businessman, a businesswoman, an entrepreneur
note: 'Pengusaha' means entrepreneur/businessperson; the root 'usaha' means effort or business, and 'berusaha' means to try hard.

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang pengusaha sukses.
sentences.en: My father is a successful businessman.

sentences.text: Dia pengusaha muda di Bali.
sentences.en: She is a young entrepreneur in Bali.

sentences.text: Banyak pengusaha buka toko di sini.
sentences.en: Many businesspeople open shops here.

note: 'Rajin' describes someone who works hard or studies diligently; often used in school or work contexts; opposite is 'malas' (lazy).

sentences.text: Dia rajin belajar setiap hari.
sentences.en: She studies diligently every day.

sentences.text: Anak itu rajin membantu orang tua.
sentences.en: That child diligently helps his parents.

sentences.text: Saya ingin lebih rajin di sekolah.
sentences.en: I want to be more hardworking at school.

english: actually, to be honest, as a matter of fact
note: 'Sebetulnya' is a common conversational word meaning 'actually' or 'to be honest'; it is interchangeable with 'sebenarnya' and used to correct or clarify something.

sentences.text: Sebetulnya saya tidak suka kopi.
sentences.en: Actually, I don't like coffee.

sentences.text: Ini sebetulnya tempat yang sangat indah.
sentences.en: This is actually a very beautiful place.

sentences.text: Sebetulnya saya sudah makan tadi.
sentences.en: To be honest, I already ate earlier.

note: 'Sepatu' means shoes (closed-toe); use 'sandal' for sandals/flip-flops — a common mix-up for beginners.

sentences.text: Saya memakai sepatu baru ke sekolah.
sentences.en: I wear new shoes to school.

sentences.text: Di mana sepatu saya?
sentences.en: Where are my shoes?

sentences.text: Sepatu ini sangat nyaman dan bagus.
sentences.en: These shoes are very comfortable and nice.

note: 'Sekretaris' means secretary or administrative assistant; used in formal and office contexts; related word: 'sekretariat' (secretariat/office).

sentences.text: Dia bekerja sebagai sekretaris di kantor.
sentences.en: She works as a secretary at the office.

sentences.text: Sekretaris itu menulis surat setiap hari.
sentences.en: The secretary writes letters every day.

sentences.text: Bu Sari adalah sekretaris yang baik.
sentences.en: Mrs. Sari is a good secretary.

note: 'Sopir' is the everyday informal word for driver (of a car, bus, or taxi); related word: 'pengemudi' is the more formal equivalent.

sentences.text: Sopir itu membawa saya ke bandara.
sentences.en: The driver took me to the airport.

sentences.text: Ayah saya bekerja sebagai sopir bus.
sentences.en: My father works as a bus driver.

sentences.text: Sopir taksi itu sangat ramah.
sentences.en: That taxi driver is very friendly.

english: a soldier, the army, the armed forces
note: 'Tentara' means soldier or the army; use 'tentara' for military personnel, not police ('polisi'); related: 'angkatan darat' (army), 'militer' (military).

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang tentara.
sentences.en: My father is a soldier.

sentences.text: Tentara itu berdiri di depan kantor.
sentences.en: The soldier is standing in front of the office.

sentences.text: Banyak tentara berlatih di lapangan.
sentences.en: Many soldiers are training on the field.

english: to answer the phone, to take a phone call
note: "Terima telepon" means to receive/answer a phone call; informally people also say "angkat telepon" (pick up the phone); used in everyday and semi-formal contexts.

sentences.text: Ibu sedang terima telepon di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is answering the phone in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Maaf, saya tidak bisa terima telepon sekarang.
sentences.en: Sorry, I cannot take a phone call right now.

sentences.text: Dia terima telepon dari temannya tadi.
sentences.en: She answered a phone call from her friend just now.

english: the things you have to do (as part of a job), a task, duties, obligations
note: "Tugas" covers schoolwork assignments, job duties, and official tasks; often confused with "pekerjaan" (general work/job), but "tugas" stresses a specific obligation or mission.

sentences.text: Saya punya tugas dari guru hari ini.
sentences.en: I have an assignment from the teacher today.

sentences.text: Tugas polisi adalah menjaga keamanan.
sentences.en: The duty of the police is to keep safety.

sentences.text: Dia belum selesai mengerjakan tugas sekolah.
sentences.en: He has not finished doing his school assignment.

note: 'Tukang kayu' literally means 'wood worker'; 'tukang' is a prefix for skilled tradespeople (e.g. tukang listrik = electrician), distinct from 'pengrajin' which implies artisan craft.

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang tukang kayu.
sentences.en: My father is a carpenter.

sentences.text: Tukang kayu itu membuat meja baru.
sentences.en: That carpenter is making a new table.

sentences.text: Kami memanggil tukang kayu ke rumah.
sentences.en: We called a carpenter to the house.

note: 'Tukang listrik' literally means 'electricity worker'; 'tukang' is a common prefix for tradespeople (e.g. tukang kayu = carpenter), used in everyday informal speech.

sentences.text: Saya memanggil tukang listrik ke rumah.
sentences.en: I called an electrician to the house.

sentences.text: Tukang listrik itu memperbaiki lampu saya.
sentences.en: The electrician fixed my light.

sentences.text: Kami butuh tukang listrik sekarang.
sentences.en: We need an electrician now.

note: "Wartawan" is a neutral, everyday word for journalist/reporter; related words include "berita" (news) and "majalah" (magazine).

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang wartawan terkenal.
sentences.en: My father is a famous journalist.

sentences.text: Wartawan itu menulis berita setiap hari.
sentences.en: That reporter writes news every day.

sentences.text: Saya ingin menjadi wartawan.
sentences.en: I want to become a journalist.

note: "Bengkel" refers to a repair shop, most commonly for vehicles; related words include "mekanik" (mechanic) and "servis" (service/repair).

sentences.text: Saya membawa motor ke bengkel.
sentences.en: I take my motorbike to the repair shop.

sentences.text: Bengkel itu dekat pasar.
sentences.en: That repair shop is near the market.

sentences.text: Mobil saya ada di bengkel.
sentences.en: My car is at the repair shop.

note: 'Ekor' means an animal's tail, but is also used as a counter/classifier for animals (like 'tiga ekor kucing' = three cats); don't use it to count people or objects.

sentences.text: Anjing itu menggoyangkan ekor dengan gembira.
sentences.en: That dog wags its tail happily.

sentences.text: Di sawah ada dua ekor bebek.
sentences.en: In the rice field there are two ducks.

sentences.text: Kucing saya punya ekor panjang.
sentences.en: My cat has a long tail.

note: 'Hadiah' is a neutral everyday word for gift or present; commonly used for birthdays and holidays; related word: 'kado' (informal gift).

sentences.text: Ini hadiah untuk ulang tahun kamu.
sentences.en: This is a gift for your birthday.

sentences.text: Dia memberi hadiah kepada adiknya.
sentences.en: She gives a gift to her younger sibling.

sentences.text: Saya suka hadiah dari ibu saya.
sentences.en: I like the gift from my mother.

english: mother, a lady, you (in addressing an elder female)
note: "Ibu" (often shortened to "Bu") means mother, but is also used as a polite title for any adult woman, similar to "Ma'am"; do not confuse with "Nyonya" (Mrs.) used in formal/written contexts.

sentences.text: Ibu memasak nasi goreng di dapur.
sentences.en: Mother is cooking fried rice in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Selamat pagi, Ibu! Apa kabar?
sentences.en: Good morning, Ma'am! How are you?

sentences.text: Ibu guru mengajar di kelas.
sentences.en: The (female) teacher is teaching in the classroom.

note: 'Kepala sekolah' literally means 'head of school'; 'kepala' also means 'head' (body part), so context matters.

sentences.text: Kepala sekolah berbicara di depan murid.
sentences.en: The school principal speaks in front of the students.

sentences.text: Ibu guru menemui kepala sekolah hari ini.
sentences.en: The teacher meets the school principal today.

sentences.text: Kepala sekolah sangat baik dan ramah.
sentences.en: The school principal is very kind and friendly.

note: 'Melukis' is the active verb form (to paint/do painting); 'lukis' is the root — related words include 'lukisan' (painting/artwork) and 'pelukis' (painter/artist).

sentences.text: Saya suka melukis pemandangan di Bali.
sentences.en: I like to paint scenery in Bali.

sentences.text: Anak itu melukis bunga dengan cat merah.
sentences.en: That child paints flowers with red paint.

sentences.text: Dia belajar melukis setiap hari Minggu.
sentences.en: She learns to paint every Sunday.

note: 'Sapi' means cow/cattle; distinguish from 'kambing' (goat) and 'kerbau' (buffalo), all common farm animals in Indonesia.

sentences.text: Petani itu punya dua ekor sapi.
sentences.en: That farmer has two cows.

sentences.text: Sapi makan rumput di ladang.
sentences.en: The cow eats grass in the field.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli daging sapi di pasar.
sentences.en: Mother buys beef at the market.

note: 'Seniman' means 'an artist/artist' (noun); related words: 'seni' (art), 'lukisan' (painting); used for any creative artist, not just painters.

sentences.text: Dia adalah seniman yang sangat berbakat.
sentences.en: He is a very talented artist.

sentences.text: Seniman itu melukis di pantai Bali.
sentences.en: The artist paints on the beach in Bali.

sentences.text: Kakak saya ingin menjadi seniman terkenal.
sentences.en: My older sibling wants to become a famous artist.

note: 'Tukang masak' is an informal term for cook/chef; more formal is 'juru masak', and 'koki' (borrowed from Dutch) is also common.

sentences.text: Tukang masak di restoran itu sangat pintar.
sentences.en: The cook at that restaurant is very skilled.

sentences.text: Ibu saya adalah tukang masak yang hebat.
sentences.en: My mother is a great cook.

sentences.text: Tukang masak itu membuat nasi goreng enak.
sentences.en: That cook makes delicious fried rice.

note: 'baru' as 'it is only then that...' follows a condition and shows the result comes after; often paired with 'kalau' or 'sudah', distinct from 'baru' meaning 'new'.

sentences.text: Sudah makan baru boleh main.
sentences.en: Only after eating can you play.

sentences.text: Kalau selesai kerja baru kita pergi.
sentences.en: Only when the work is done will we go.

sentences.text: Bayar dulu baru masuk.
sentences.en: Pay first, only then you may enter.

note: 'Habis' means something is used up or all gone; also informally means 'after/then' (e.g. habis makan), and is related to 'kehabisan' (run out of).

sentences.text: Airnya sudah habis, tolong beli lagi.
sentences.en: The water is all gone, please buy more.

sentences.text: Nasinya habis karena tamu banyak.
sentences.en: The rice is all gone because there were many guests.

sentences.text: Uang saya habis di pasar tadi.
sentences.en: My money ran out at the market just now.

note: 'Jarang' means rarely/seldom; opposite is 'sering' (often); used before verbs just like in English.

sentences.text: Saya jarang makan di restoran mahal.
sentences.en: I rarely eat at expensive restaurants.

sentences.text: Dia jarang pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: She rarely goes to the beach.

sentences.text: Kami jarang minum kopi pagi ini.
sentences.en: We rarely drink coffee in the morning.

note: 'Kue kering' literally means 'dry cake' and refers to cookies or biscuits; contrast with 'kue basah' (moist/wet snacks like sticky rice cakes).

sentences.text: Ibu membuat kue kering untuk Lebaran.
sentences.en: Mom makes cookies for Eid.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan kue kering cokelat.
sentences.en: I like eating chocolate cookies.

sentences.text: Toko itu menjual kue kering yang enak.
sentences.en: That shop sells delicious biscuits.

note: "Makanan kecil" literally means "small food" and is a common informal term for snacks; similar to "camilan" which is also widely used in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan makanan kecil sore hari.
sentences.en: I like to eat snacks in the afternoon.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli makanan kecil di pasar.
sentences.en: Mother bought snacks at the market.

sentences.text: Anak-anak senang makan makanan kecil ini.
sentences.en: The children enjoy eating these snacks.

note: 'Mengurus' is the formal/active form of 'urus'; commonly used for handling paperwork, caring for family, or managing tasks — not to be confused with 'merawat' which implies nurturing/physical care.

sentences.text: Ibu mengurus semua keperluan di rumah.
sentences.en: Mom takes care of all the needs at home.

sentences.text: Dia mengurus dokumen di kantor hari ini.
sentences.en: He takes care of the documents at the office today.

sentences.text: Saya harus mengurus adik saya besok.
sentences.en: I have to take care of my younger sibling tomorrow.

note: 'Organisasi' is a formal loanword from Dutch/English, used for clubs, NGOs, or structured groups; beginners may also hear 'kelompok' for smaller informal groups.

sentences.text: Dia bergabung dengan organisasi sosial di desa.
sentences.en: She joined a social organisation in the village.

sentences.text: Organisasi itu membantu anak-anak miskin.
sentences.en: The organisation helps poor children.

sentences.text: Saya ingin masuk organisasi pemuda ini.
sentences.en: I want to join this youth organisation.

note: 'Pembangunan' means development/construction; root word 'bangun' also means 'to wake up' or 'to build'; commonly used for infrastructure or national development projects.

sentences.text: Pembangunan jalan baru sudah selesai.
sentences.en: The construction of the new road is finished.

sentences.text: Kami melihat pembangunan gedung besar itu.
sentences.en: We saw the construction of that big building.

sentences.text: Pembangunan desa ini sangat bagus.
sentences.en: The development of this village is very good.

note: 'Program' is borrowed directly from English and is widely used in Indonesian for plans, schedules, or organized activities; also seen as 'acara' for events.

sentences.text: Program liburan kami sangat menyenangkan.
sentences.en: Our holiday plan is very fun.

sentences.text: Apa program kamu hari ini?
sentences.en: What is your plan for today?

sentences.text: Program desa ini sangat bagus.
sentences.en: This village program is very good.

note: "Rapat" means a formal or informal meeting/gathering; also means "tight/close together" — context clarifies which meaning is intended.

sentences.text: Saya ada rapat di kantor hari ini.
sentences.en: I have a meeting at the office today.

sentences.text: Rapat itu mulai jam sembilan pagi.
sentences.en: The meeting starts at nine in the morning.

sentences.text: Ibu guru ikut rapat bersama kepala sekolah.
sentences.en: The teacher joined a meeting with the principal.

note: 'Sambal' is a common spicy condiment/paste served with most Indonesian meals; often confused with general 'chili' (cabai), but sambal is always a prepared dish.

sentences.text: Saya suka makan nasi dengan sambal.
sentences.en: I like eating rice with chili paste.

sentences.text: Sambal ini sangat pedas sekali.
sentences.en: This chili paste is very spicy.

sentences.text: Ibu membuat sambal di dapur.
sentences.en: Mom is making chili paste in the kitchen.

note: "Sedikit" means a small amount or few of something; often confused with "sedikit-sedikit" (little by little); related: "banyak" (a lot) is its opposite.

sentences.text: Saya mau sedikit nasi, terima kasih.
sentences.en: I want a little rice, thank you.

sentences.text: Dia bisa berbicara sedikit bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: She can speak a little Indonesian.

sentences.text: Ada sedikit air di botol itu.
sentences.en: There is a little water in that bottle.

note: 'Urusan' refers to personal or business matters/affairs; slightly formal but very common; related: 'masalah' (problem), 'keperluan' (needs)

sentences.text: Saya punya urusan penting di kantor.
sentences.en: I have important matters at the office.

sentences.text: Dia sibuk dengan urusan keluarganya.
sentences.en: She is busy with her family affairs.

sentences.text: Itu bukan urusan kamu.
sentences.en: That is not your business.

note: 'Berwawancara' is a formal verb meaning to conduct or give an interview; commonly used in job or journalism contexts; related to 'wawancara' (interview/noun).

sentences.text: Dia berwawancara dengan manajer hotel hari ini.
sentences.en: He is conducting an interview with the hotel manager today.

sentences.text: Saya berwawancara untuk pekerjaan baru kemarin.
sentences.en: I had an interview for a new job yesterday.

sentences.text: Wartawan itu berwawancara dengan kepala desa.
sentences.en: The journalist is conducting an interview with the village head.

note: 'Masalah' means 'problem' or 'issue'; common in both formal and informal speech; related words: 'bermasalah' (problematic), 'tidak masalah' (no problem/it's okay).

sentences.text: Saya punya masalah dengan motor saya.
sentences.en: I have a problem with my motorbike.

sentences.text: Tidak ada masalah di sini.
sentences.en: There is no problem here.

sentences.text: Apa masalah kamu hari ini?
sentences.en: What is your problem today?

note: 'Membangun' is the active transitive form (me- prefix on 'bangun'); 'bangun' alone also means 'to wake up/rise', so context matters.

sentences.text: Mereka membangun rumah baru di sini.
sentences.en: They are building a new house here.

sentences.text: Ayah ingin membangun toko kecil.
sentences.en: Dad wants to build a small shop.

english: to try to find a way
note: 'Mencari jalan' literally means 'to search for a road/way'; used figuratively for finding a solution, common in everyday problem-solving contexts; related: 'jalan keluar' (way out/solution)

sentences.text: Kami mencari jalan ke pantai itu.
sentences.en: We are trying to find a way to that beach.

sentences.text: Dia mencari jalan untuk pulang ke rumah.
sentences.en: He is trying to find a way to go home.

sentences.text: Mereka mencari jalan keluar dari masalah.
sentences.en: They are trying to find a way out of the problem.

note: 'Orang desa' literally means 'village person'; used neutrally, not offensive; related: 'orang kota' (city person), 'desa' (village)

sentences.text: Dia adalah orang desa yang ramah.
sentences.en: He is a friendly villager.

sentences.text: Orang desa itu menjual sayuran segar.
sentences.en: That villager sells fresh vegetables.

sentences.text: Saya bertemu orang desa di pasar.
sentences.en: I met a villager at the market.

english: after (a more formal variant of sesudah)
note: 'Setelah' means 'after' and is slightly more formal than 'sesudah'; both are common in written and spoken Indonesian.

sentences.text: Saya mandi setelah pulang dari pantai.
sentences.en: I shower after coming home from the beach.

sentences.text: Setelah makan, kami minum kopi.
sentences.en: After eating, we drink coffee.

note: 'Abjad' means alphabet or set of letters; used in formal and school contexts; sometimes confused with 'huruf' (a single letter).

sentences.text: Anak-anak belajar abjad di sekolah.
sentences.en: Children learn the alphabet at school.

sentences.text: Ada dua puluh enam abjad dalam bahasa Inggris.
sentences.en: There are twenty-six letters in the English alphabet.

sentences.text: Ibu mengajar abjad kepada adik.
sentences.en: Mom teaches the alphabet to my younger sibling.

note: 'Ejaan' means spelling/orthography; often heard in school contexts; related: 'mengeja' (to spell out), 'huruf' (letter)

sentences.text: Ejaan kata ini salah di bukumu.
sentences.en: The spelling of this word is wrong in your book.

sentences.text: Ibu guru mengecek ejaan tulisan saya.
sentences.en: The teacher checks the spelling of my writing.

sentences.text: Saya belajar ejaan bahasa Indonesia hari ini.
sentences.en: I am learning Indonesian spelling today.

note: 'Huruf' means a letter of the alphabet; not to be confused with 'surat' (a written letter/mail); related: 'huruf besar' (capital letter), 'huruf kecil' (lowercase letter).

sentences.text: Saya belajar huruf A sampai Z.
sentences.en: I am learning the letters A to Z.

sentences.text: Huruf pertama nama saya adalah D.
sentences.en: The first letter of my name is D.

sentences.text: Tulis huruf ini di buku kamu.
sentences.en: Write this letter in your book.

note: 'Khusus' means 'special' or 'specific'; often used before nouns like 'khusus untuk' (especially for); don't confuse with 'spesial' which is also used but more informal/borrowed.

sentences.text: Ini tempat parkir khusus untuk motor.
sentences.en: This is a parking spot specifically for motorcycles.

sentences.text: Ada menu khusus untuk anak-anak.
sentences.en: There is a special menu for children.

sentences.text: Kamar ini khusus untuk tamu VIP.
sentences.en: This room is specifically for VIP guests.

note: 'Peneliti' means researcher/scientist; comes from root 'teliti' (careful/thorough); related: 'meneliti' (to research), 'penelitian' (research).

sentences.text: Ibu saya adalah seorang peneliti di sini.
sentences.en: My mother is a researcher here.

sentences.text: Peneliti itu bekerja di laboratorium setiap hari.
sentences.en: That researcher works in the laboratory every day.

sentences.text: Dia ingin menjadi peneliti terkenal.
sentences.en: She wants to become a famous researcher.

note: "Sekali lagi" means "once more/again" and is used in everyday speech; don't confuse with "lagi" alone (which can mean "again" or "more" informally) or "sekali" alone (which means "once" or "very").

sentences.text: Tolong ucapkan sekali lagi, pak.
sentences.en: Please say it once more, sir.

sentences.text: Saya mau mencoba sekali lagi.
sentences.en: I want to try once more.

sentences.text: Boleh saya lihat sekali lagi?
sentences.en: May I see it once more?

note: 'Terima kasih kembali' is a polite, slightly formal reply to 'thank you'; the shorter 'sama-sama' is more common in casual speech.

sentences.text: Terima kasih kembali atas bantuannya, Pak.
sentences.en: You're welcome for your help, Sir.

sentences.text: Oh, terima kasih kembali, Bu Made.
sentences.en: Oh, you're welcome, Mrs. Made.

sentences.text: Terima kasih kembali, semoga harimu menyenangkan.
sentences.en: You're welcome, I hope your day is pleasant.

note: 'Tulisan' means writing or a piece of writing; related to 'tulis' (to write); not to be confused with 'tulisan tangan' (handwriting) specifically.

sentences.text: Tulisan kamu sangat bagus dan rapi.
sentences.en: Your writing is very good and neat.

sentences.text: Saya tidak bisa membaca tulisan ini.
sentences.en: I cannot read this writing.

sentences.text: Tulisan di papan itu besar sekali.
sentences.en: The writing on that board is very big.

note: 'Ucapan' can mean both 'pronunciation' and 'utterance/expression' (e.g., ucapan selamat = congratulatory greeting); beginners should note context determines the meaning.

sentences.text: Ucapan kamu dalam bahasa Bali sangat bagus.
sentences.en: Your pronunciation in Balinese is very good.

sentences.text: Tolong perbaiki ucapan kata ini.
sentences.en: Please correct the pronunciation of this word.

sentences.text: Ucapan yang benar sangat penting.
sentences.en: Correct pronunciation is very important.

note: 'Atas' means 'above' or 'on top of'; often confused with 'di atas' (on top of/above) when used as a preposition — beginners should note it commonly pairs with 'di'.

sentences.text: Buku itu ada di atas meja.
sentences.en: The book is on top of the table.

sentences.text: Kucing duduk di atas kursi.
sentences.en: The cat sits on top of the chair.

sentences.text: Pesawat terbang di atas awan.
sentences.en: The airplane flies above the clouds.

note: 'Bawah' means 'below/under'; common phrase 'di bawah' means 'underneath'; opposite is 'atas' (above/top).

sentences.text: Kucing itu tidur di bawah meja.
sentences.en: The cat sleeps under the table.

sentences.text: Sandal saya ada di bawah kursi.
sentences.en: My sandals are under the chair.

sentences.text: Tolong lihat di bawah tempat tidur.
sentences.en: Please look under the bed.

note: 'Berbeda' means 'different'; use it with 'dari' (from) to compare, e.g. 'berbeda dari'; related: 'beda' (informal short form), 'perbedaan' (difference)

sentences.text: Warna baju kita berbeda sekali.
sentences.en: The color of our clothes is very different.

sentences.text: Rasa makanan ini berbeda dari kemarin.
sentences.en: The taste of this food is different from yesterday.

sentences.text: Pendapat kami berbeda, tapi tidak apa-apa.
sentences.en: Our opinions are different, but that is okay.

note: 'Dasar' means 'basic' or 'foundation'; also used informally as a mild exclamation (e.g. 'dasar!' = 'typical!'); related: 'dasarnya' (basically), 'mendasar' (fundamental).

sentences.text: Ini adalah kelas bahasa Indonesia dasar.
sentences.en: This is a basic Indonesian language class.

sentences.text: Dasar resep ini adalah santan kelapa.
sentences.en: The foundation of this recipe is coconut milk.

sentences.text: Saya belajar kata-kata dasar dulu.
sentences.en: I study basic words first.

note: 'Dunia' means 'world' and is used in everyday speech; common in phrases like 'seluruh dunia' (the whole world); related words: 'dunia nyata' (real world).

sentences.text: Bali terkenal di seluruh dunia.
sentences.en: Bali is famous throughout the whole world.

sentences.text: Saya ingin keliling dunia suatu hari.
sentences.en: I want to travel around the world someday.

sentences.text: Dunia ini sangat indah dan luas.
sentences.en: This world is very beautiful and vast.

note: 'Hal' means 'matter/thing/topic'; often used in 'hal ini' (this matter) or 'banyak hal' (many things); similar to but more formal than 'sesuatu'.

sentences.text: Ini adalah hal yang penting.
sentences.en: This is an important matter.

sentences.text: Ada banyak hal di pasar.
sentences.en: There are many things at the market.

sentences.text: Hal ini mudah untuk dipelajari.
sentences.en: This matter is easy to learn.

note: 'Ilmu pengetahuan' means science or knowledge; often shortened to 'ilmu' in casual speech; not to be confused with 'sains' which is used for natural/school science subjects.

sentences.text: Dia suka belajar ilmu pengetahuan di sekolah.
sentences.en: She likes studying science at school.

sentences.text: Ilmu pengetahuan sangat penting untuk kehidupan.
sentences.en: Science is very important for life.

sentences.text: Buku ilmu pengetahuan ada di perpustakaan.
sentences.en: The science book is in the library.

note: 'Kejuruan' means vocational/trade-based; commonly seen in 'SMK' (Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan), Indonesia's vocational high school; do not confuse with 'akademik' (academic).

sentences.text: Dia belajar di sekolah kejuruan.
sentences.en: He studies at a vocational school.

sentences.text: Sekolah kejuruan mengajarkan banyak keterampilan.
sentences.en: Vocational school teaches many skills.

sentences.text: Adik saya masuk sekolah kejuruan.
sentences.en: My younger sibling enrolled in a vocational school.

note: 'Kurang banyak' means 'too few' or 'not enough in quantity'; often confused with 'kurang' alone (just 'not enough'); related: 'terlalu sedikit' (too little).

sentences.text: Kursinya kurang banyak untuk semua tamu.
sentences.en: The chairs are too few for all the guests.

sentences.text: Airnya kurang banyak di botol ini.
sentences.en: The water is not enough in this bottle.

sentences.text: Makanan di piring itu kurang banyak.
sentences.en: The food on that plate is too little.

note: "Kurikulum" is a formal/academic loanword from Dutch/English; used in school and education contexts, related words: 'pelajaran' (subject/lesson), 'sekolah' (school).

sentences.text: Sekolah kami menggunakan kurikulum baru tahun ini.
sentences.en: Our school uses a new curriculum this year.

sentences.text: Kurikulum di sekolah itu sangat bagus.
sentences.en: The curriculum at that school is very good.

sentences.text: Guru menjelaskan kurikulum kepada orang tua.
sentences.en: The teacher explained the curriculum to the parents.

note: "Lebih dulu" means doing something before others or before another action; often confused with "pertama" (first in order/sequence) — use "lebih dulu" when comparing who does something earlier.

sentences.text: Saya makan lebih dulu sebelum pergi.
sentences.en: I eat first before going.

sentences.text: Dia datang lebih dulu dari saya.
sentences.en: She arrived earlier than me.

sentences.text: Ayo tidur lebih dulu, sudah malam.
sentences.en: Let's sleep first, it's already night.

note: 'Mata pelajaran' means school subject; 'mata' alone means 'eye', so always use the full phrase for subject context.

sentences.text: Mata pelajaran favorit saya adalah matematika.
sentences.en: My favorite subject is mathematics.

sentences.text: Ada berapa mata pelajaran hari ini?
sentences.en: How many subjects are there today?

sentences.text: Saya suka mata pelajaran bahasa Inggris.
sentences.en: I like the subject English.

note: 'Milik' means 'belonging of' or 'owned by'; often used in phrases like 'milik saya' (mine) or 'milik negara' (state-owned); do not confuse with 'punya' which is a verb meaning 'to have/own'.

sentences.text: Buku ini milik saya.
sentences.en: This book belongs to me.

sentences.text: Tas itu milik siapa?
sentences.en: Whose bag is that?

sentences.text: Rumah besar itu milik pak Budi.
sentences.en: That big house belongs to Mr. Budi.

note: "Muatan lokal" refers to locally-adapted school subjects (e.g., Balinese culture, batik); commonly used in Indonesian education contexts; related: "pelajaran" (lesson), "kurikulum" (curriculum).

sentences.text: Sekolah kami ada pelajaran muatan lokal.
sentences.en: Our school has a local content subject.

sentences.text: Muatan lokal di Bali adalah bahasa Bali.
sentences.en: The local content in Bali is Balinese language.

sentences.text: Saya suka kelas muatan lokal hari ini.
sentences.en: I like the local content class today.

note: "Negeri" means state-owned or government-run; commonly used in "sekolah negeri" (public school) vs "sekolah swasta" (private school); not to be confused with "negara" (nation/country).

sentences.text: Adik saya belajar di sekolah negeri.
sentences.en: My younger sibling studies at a public school.

sentences.text: Rumah sakit negeri itu dekat pasar.
sentences.en: That government hospital is near the market.

sentences.text: Dia kerja di kantor negeri.
sentences.en: She works at a government office.

note: 'Pendidikan' means education as a concept or system; 'didik' is the root verb meaning to educate/raise; commonly seen in school and formal contexts.

sentences.text: Pendidikan sangat penting untuk masa depan.
sentences.en: Education is very important for the future.

sentences.text: Anak itu mendapat pendidikan yang baik.
sentences.en: That child receives a good education.

sentences.text: Di Bali, pendidikan gratis untuk semua.
sentences.en: In Bali, education is free for everyone.

note: 'Sebagian besar' means 'most' or 'the majority of'; more formal than 'kebanyakan' but both are common; used before nouns.

sentences.text: Sebagian besar teman saya suka nasi goreng.
sentences.en: Most of my friends like fried rice.

sentences.text: Sebagian besar turis pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: Most tourists go to the beach.

sentences.text: Sebagian besar anak minum air putih.
sentences.en: Most children drink plain water.

note: 'Sistem' is a neutral loanword from English/Dutch, used in formal and everyday speech; no common confusion, related: 'sistematis' (systematic).

sentences.text: Sistem internet di sini sangat lambat.
sentences.en: The internet system here is very slow.

sentences.text: Kami belajar sistem baru di sekolah.
sentences.en: We are learning a new system at school.

sentences.text: Sistem pembayaran ini mudah digunakan.
sentences.en: This payment system is easy to use.

note: 'Tanaman' means plant (noun); related words: 'menanam' (to plant), 'tanah' (soil); commonly used for garden or potted plants in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya suka merawat tanaman di rumah.
sentences.en: I like taking care of plants at home.

sentences.text: Tanaman ini butuh banyak air.
sentences.en: This plant needs a lot of water.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli tanaman baru kemarin.
sentences.en: Mom bought a new plant yesterday.

note: 'Termasuk' means 'included in' or 'including'; commonly used in shopping and menus; do not confuse with 'termasuk' (to include) vs 'mencakup' (to cover/encompass)

sentences.text: Harga ini termasuk sarapan pagi.
sentences.en: This price includes breakfast.

sentences.text: Apakah minuman termasuk dalam paket ini?
sentences.en: Are drinks included in this package?

sentences.text: Semua orang termasuk anak-anak boleh masuk.
sentences.en: Everyone including children may enter.

note: 'Tingkat' means 'level' or 'floor/storey'; commonly used for difficulty levels, school grades, and building floors.

sentences.text: Bahasa Indonesia tingkat satu mudah dipelajari.
sentences.en: Level one Indonesian is easy to learn.

sentences.text: Hotel ini punya tiga tingkat.
sentences.en: This hotel has three floors.

sentences.text: Saya belajar di tingkat dua.
sentences.en: I study on the second floor.

note: "Umum" means public or general; used in phrases like "toilet umum" (public toilet) or "pengetahuan umum" (general knowledge); not to be confused with "publik" which is a loanword used in formal contexts.

sentences.text: Di mana toilet umum di sini?
sentences.en: Where is the public toilet here?

sentences.text: Bus umum itu murah sekali.
sentences.en: The public bus is very cheap.

sentences.text: Ini informasi umum untuk semua orang.
sentences.en: This is general information for everyone.

note: 'Berguna' means 'useful/beneficial'; related to 'guna' (use/benefit); common in everyday speech, slightly more formal than 'bermanfaat'.

sentences.text: Kamus ini sangat berguna untuk belajar bahasa.
sentences.en: This dictionary is very useful for learning language.

sentences.text: Sepeda berguna untuk pergi ke pasar.
sentences.en: A bicycle is useful for going to the market.

sentences.text: Aplikasi ini berguna setiap hari.
sentences.en: This app is useful every day.

note: 'Berkebun' means 'to garden/do gardening'; it uses the 'ber-' prefix to show an activity, similar to 'berenang' (to swim) or 'berlari' (to run).

sentences.text: Ibu suka berkebun di halaman rumah.
sentences.en: Mom likes to garden in the yard.

sentences.text: Saya berkebun setiap pagi bersama ayah.
sentences.en: I garden every morning with my father.

sentences.text: Mereka berkebun untuk menanam sayuran segar.
sentences.en: They garden to grow fresh vegetables.

note: "Bersifat" means 'to be (of a certain nature/character)'; often used before adjectives to describe inherent qualities; related to "sifat" (nature, trait).

sentences.text: Air laut bersifat asin dan segar.
sentences.en: Sea water is salty and fresh in nature.

sentences.text: Kegiatan ini bersifat bebas untuk semua.
sentences.en: This activity is free in nature for everyone.

sentences.text: Anjing itu bersifat ramah dan lucu.
sentences.en: That dog is friendly and cute in character.

note: "Cara" means "way" or "method"; often used in phrases like "cara ini" (this way) or "cara memasak" (way of cooking); not to be confused with "jalan" which means road/path.

sentences.text: Apa cara terbaik untuk belajar bahasa?
sentences.en: What is the best way to learn a language?

sentences.text: Saya suka cara kamu memasak nasi.
sentences.en: I like the way you cook rice.

sentences.text: Ini cara mudah membuat kopi.
sentences.en: This is an easy way to make coffee.

note: 'Fisika' means physics (the science subject); used in school contexts, related words: 'kimia' (chemistry), 'biologi' (biology), 'pelajaran' (lesson/subject).

sentences.text: Saya suka pelajaran fisika di sekolah.
sentences.en: I like physics class at school.

sentences.text: Fisika itu susah tapi menarik.
sentences.en: Physics is difficult but interesting.

sentences.text: Guru fisika saya sangat baik.
sentences.en: My physics teacher is very kind.

note: 'Hasil' means result or yield; common in school (exam results) and farming (harvest yield); related: 'hasilkan' (to produce).

sentences.text: Hasil ujiannya sangat bagus hari ini.
sentences.en: The exam result is very good today.

sentences.text: Petani itu senang dengan hasil panennya.
sentences.en: The farmer is happy with his harvest yield.

sentences.text: Apa hasil kerja kamu kemarin?
sentences.en: What was the result of your work yesterday?

note: 'Kambing' means goat; commonly seen on menus as 'sate kambing' (goat satay); not to be confused with 'domba' (sheep).

sentences.text: Saya melihat kambing di ladang itu.
sentences.en: I see a goat in that field.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli daging kambing di pasar.
sentences.en: Mother buys goat meat at the market.

sentences.text: Kambing itu makan rumput setiap hari.
sentences.en: The goat eats grass every day.

note: 'Kerbau' means water buffalo, a common farm animal in rural Indonesia; not to be confused with 'sapi' (cow) or 'kambing' (goat).

sentences.text: Kerbau itu makan rumput di sawah.
sentences.en: The water buffalo eats grass in the rice field.

sentences.text: Pak tani punya satu kerbau besar.
sentences.en: The farmer has one big water buffalo.

sentences.text: Anak-anak melihat kerbau di ladang.
sentences.en: The children see a water buffalo in the field.

note: 'Keterampilan' is a formal/neutral noun for 'skill' or 'ability'; related to 'terampil' (skillful); more specific than 'kemampuan' (general ability).

sentences.text: Dia punya keterampilan memasak yang bagus.
sentences.en: She has good cooking skills.

sentences.text: Keterampilan berenang sangat penting untuk anak.
sentences.en: Swimming skills are very important for children.

sentences.text: Saya ingin belajar keterampilan baru hari ini.
sentences.en: I want to learn a new skill today.

note: 'Menengah' means middle-level (e.g. school, income); 'tengah' alone means 'middle/center' as a position — both share the same root.

sentences.text: Dia belajar di sekolah menengah sekarang.
sentences.en: He/She studies at a middle school now.

sentences.text: Rumah saya ada di tengah jalan.
sentences.en: My house is in the middle of the road.

sentences.text: Warung itu ada di tengah pasar.
sentences.en: That food stall is in the middle of the market.

note: 'Mesin cuci' literally means 'wash machine'; commonly used in everyday Indonesian for washing machine, distinct from 'mesin' (machine) alone.

sentences.text: Saya mencuci baju dengan mesin cuci.
sentences.en: I wash clothes with the washing machine.

sentences.text: Mesin cuci ada di kamar mandi.
sentences.en: The washing machine is in the bathroom.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli mesin cuci baru kemarin.
sentences.en: Mom bought a new washing machine yesterday.

note: 'Mesin' means both 'engine' and 'machine'; commonly used in everyday contexts like motorbikes, washing machines, and ATMs.

sentences.text: Mesin motor saya rusak kemarin.
sentences.en: My motorbike engine broke down yesterday.

sentences.text: Ibu mencuci baju dengan mesin cuci.
sentences.en: Mom washes clothes with a washing machine.

sentences.text: Mesin ATM ada di depan minimarket.
sentences.en: The ATM machine is in front of the minimarket.

note: "Para" is placed before a noun to indicate a group of people; never used for animals or objects, and differs from "semua" (all/every).

sentences.text: Para siswa belajar di kelas hari ini.
sentences.en: The students are studying in class today.

sentences.text: Para turis mengunjungi Pura Besakih kemarin.
sentences.en: The tourists visited Besakih Temple yesterday.

sentences.text: Para ibu memasak makanan di dapur.
sentences.en: The mothers are cooking food in the kitchen.

note: 'Pertanian' means agriculture or farming; related words include 'petani' (farmer) and 'bertani' (to farm); common in rural Indonesian contexts.

sentences.text: Bali terkenal dengan pertanian sawah yang indah.
sentences.en: Bali is famous for its beautiful rice field agriculture.

sentences.text: Ayah saya bekerja di bidang pertanian.
sentences.en: My father works in the field of agriculture.

sentences.text: Pertanian padi sangat penting di Indonesia.
sentences.en: Rice agriculture is very important in Indonesia.

note: 'Siswa' refers to a school student (elementary to high school); 'mahasiswa' is used for university students — don't mix them up.

sentences.text: Siswa itu pergi ke sekolah setiap hari.
sentences.en: That student goes to school every day.

sentences.text: Ibu guru memanggil nama siswa baru.
sentences.en: The teacher calls the new student's name.

sentences.text: Ada dua puluh siswa di kelas ini.
sentences.en: There are twenty students in this class.

note: 'Usaha tani' means a farming or agricultural enterprise/business; common in rural Indonesia, sometimes written as one word 'usahatani'; related to 'petani' (farmer) and 'pertanian' (agriculture).

sentences.text: Pak Wayan memiliki usaha tani yang sukses.
sentences.en: Pak Wayan has a successful agricultural enterprise.

sentences.text: Usaha tani kami menghasilkan banyak beras.
sentences.en: Our agricultural enterprise produces a lot of rice.

sentences.text: Dia belajar tentang usaha tani di sekolah.
sentences.en: He learns about agricultural enterprise at school.

note: 'Berbagai' means 'various/many kinds of' and is used before nouns; similar to 'bermacam-macam' but shorter and more common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Pasar ini menjual berbagai buah segar.
sentences.en: This market sells various fresh fruits.

sentences.text: Ada berbagai makanan enak di sini.
sentences.en: There are various delicious foods here.

sentences.text: Bali punya berbagai pantai yang indah.
sentences.en: Bali has various beautiful beaches.

note: 'Bersama-sama' means 'together' and is slightly more emphatic than 'bersama'; both are common, but 'bersama-sama' often implies doing something as a group.

sentences.text: Kita makan bersama-sama di rumah.
sentences.en: We eat together at home.

sentences.text: Anak-anak bermain bersama-sama di pantai.
sentences.en: The children play together at the beach.

note: Formal term for 'natural science' (often abbreviated 'IPA' in schools); used in academic contexts; related: 'ilmu sosial' (social science), 'pelajaran' (lesson/subject).

sentences.text: Saya suka pelajaran ilmu pengetahuan alam.
sentences.en: I like the natural science subject.

sentences.text: Ilmu pengetahuan alam sangat menarik bagi saya.
sentences.en: Natural science is very interesting to me.

sentences.text: Buku ilmu pengetahuan alam ada di meja.
sentences.en: The natural science book is on the table.

note: Formal term for 'social studies/science'; often abbreviated as 'IPS' in Indonesian schools; related: 'ilmu pengetahuan alam' (IPA) for natural science.

sentences.text: Saya suka pelajaran ilmu pengetahuan sosial di sekolah.
sentences.en: I like social science class at school.

sentences.text: Buku ilmu pengetahuan sosial ada di meja.
sentences.en: The social science book is on the table.

note: 'Pada waktu itu' means 'at that time'; slightly formal, often used in storytelling; related: 'saat itu' (same meaning, more casual)

sentences.text: Pada waktu itu, saya tinggal di Bali.
sentences.en: At that time, I lived in Bali.

sentences.text: Pada waktu itu, toko sudah tutup.
sentences.en: At that time, the shop was already closed.

sentences.text: Dia masih anak-anak pada waktu itu.
sentences.en: He was still a child at that time.

note: SMA is the standard abbreviation for Indonesian high school (grades 10–12); often used alone as 'SMA' in everyday speech; related terms include SD (elementary) and SMP (middle school).

sentences.text: Adik saya belajar di Sekolah Menengah Atas.
sentences.en: My younger sibling studies at high school.

sentences.text: Dia ingin masuk Sekolah Menengah Atas negeri.
sentences.en: He wants to enter a public high school.

note: 'Ahli' means expert or specialist; commonly used before a noun (e.g., ahli masak = cooking expert); not to be confused with 'pandai' (smart/clever).

sentences.text: Dia adalah ahli memasak yang terkenal.
sentences.en: He is a famous cooking expert.

sentences.text: Ayah saya seorang ahli dokter gigi.
sentences.en: My father is a dental specialist.

sentences.text: Kami butuh ahli untuk pekerjaan ini.
sentences.en: We need an expert for this job.

note: 'Bibi' means aunt (parent's sister); 'tante' is also common, especially in urban/formal contexts.

sentences.text: Bibi saya tinggal di Bali.
sentences.en: My aunt lives in Bali.

sentences.text: Saya makan siang dengan bibi.
sentences.en: I have lunch with my aunt.

sentences.text: Bibi membeli buah di pasar.
sentences.en: My aunt buys fruit at the market.

note: Used in academic and news contexts; 'pertanian' means farming/agriculture, often confused with 'perkebunan' (plantation); related: 'petani' (farmer), 'hasil pertanian' (farm produce).

sentences.text: Dia belajar ekonomi pertanian di universitas.
sentences.en: He studies agricultural economics at university.

sentences.text: Ekonomi pertanian Bali sangat penting.
sentences.en: Bali's agricultural economy is very important.

sentences.text: Pak Wayan memahami ekonomi pertanian dengan baik.
sentences.en: Mr. Wayan understands agricultural economics well.

english: degree, professional title, title of respect
note: 'Gelar' means academic degree (S1, S2) or honorary/professional title; not to be confused with 'judul' (title of a book/film).

sentences.text: Dia sudah mendapat gelar dokter tahun ini.
sentences.en: He already received his doctor's degree this year.

sentences.text: Apa gelar kamu setelah lulus kuliah?
sentences.en: What is your degree after you graduate from university?

sentences.text: Pak Budi punya gelar sarjana ekonomi.
sentences.en: Mr. Budi has a bachelor's degree in economics.

note: 'Katolik' refers to the Catholic religion; related words include 'gereja Katolik' (Catholic church) and 'Kristen' (Christian, often used for Protestant).

sentences.text: Dia pergi ke gereja Katolik setiap Minggu.
sentences.en: She goes to the Catholic church every Sunday.

sentences.text: Teman saya beragama Katolik.
sentences.en: My friend is Catholic.

note: "yang ke-" marks ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, etc.); attach a number directly after the hyphen, e.g. "yang ke-3"; often confused with cardinal numbers — don't drop "yang ke-" when ranking order.

sentences.text: Ini adalah lomba yang ke-3 saya.
sentences.en: This is my 3rd competition.

sentences.text: Dia tiba yang ke-2 di garis finish.
sentences.en: He arrived 2nd at the finish line.

sentences.text: Hari ini adalah hari yang ke-7.
sentences.en: Today is the 7th day.

note: 'Laboratorium' is a formal/neutral word used in schools and hospitals; often shortened to 'lab' in casual speech.

sentences.text: Kami belajar sains di laboratorium sekolah.
sentences.en: We study science in the school laboratory.

sentences.text: Laboratorium ini bersih dan besar.
sentences.en: This laboratory is clean and big.

sentences.text: Dokter bekerja di laboratorium rumah sakit.
sentences.en: The doctor works in the hospital laboratory.

note: 'Mengatakan' is formal/written; in everyday speech Indonesians often use 'bilang' instead; 'katakan' is the imperative or base form.

sentences.text: Dia mengatakan bahwa dia lapar.
sentences.en: He/She says that he/she is hungry.

sentences.text: Ibu mengatakan selamat pagi kepada saya.
sentences.en: Mom says good morning to me.

sentences.text: Tolong katakan namamu kepada guru.
sentences.en: Please say your name to the teacher.

note: 'Paman' means uncle (parent's brother); informal alternative is 'om', often used for older male family friends too.

sentences.text: Paman saya tinggal di Bali.
sentences.en: My uncle lives in Bali.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke pasar dengan paman.
sentences.en: I go to the market with my uncle.

sentences.text: Paman membeli nasi goreng untuk saya.
sentences.en: My uncle buys fried rice for me.

note: 'Sarjana' means a university graduate (bachelor's degree holder); often used in job ads; related: 'gelar sarjana' (bachelor's degree), not to be confused with 'pelajar' (student).

sentences.text: Kakak saya sudah menjadi sarjana tahun ini.
sentences.en: My older sibling became a university graduate this year.

sentences.text: Dia mencari kerja sebagai sarjana baru.
sentences.en: He is looking for work as a new graduate.

sentences.text: Orang tua saya bangga karena saya sarjana.
sentences.en: My parents are proud because I am a university graduate.

note: 'Sosiologi' is a formal academic word used in school/university contexts; related to 'sosial' (social) and 'masyarakat' (society).

sentences.text: Saya belajar sosiologi di universitas.
sentences.en: I study sociology at university.

sentences.text: Buku sosiologi ini sangat menarik.
sentences.en: This sociology book is very interesting.

sentences.text: Guru sosiologi kami sangat baik.
sentences.en: Our sociology teacher is very kind.

note: "Teknik mesin" is the standard Indonesian term for the university major 'mechanical engineering'; often shortened to 'tekmesin' in casual speech.

sentences.text: Saya ingin kuliah teknik mesin di Bali.
sentences.en: I want to study mechanical engineering in Bali.

sentences.text: Kakak saya lulus dari teknik mesin.
sentences.en: My older sibling graduated from mechanical engineering.

sentences.text: Teknik mesin adalah jurusan yang susah.
sentences.en: Mechanical engineering is a difficult major.

note: 'Teknik pertanian' refers to agricultural engineering or farming techniques; used in academic and rural contexts; related words: 'pertanian' (farming), 'petani' (farmer).

sentences.text: Dia belajar teknik pertanian di sekolah.
sentences.en: He studies agricultural engineering at school.

sentences.text: Teknik pertanian membantu petani bekerja lebih mudah.
sentences.en: Agricultural engineering helps farmers work more easily.

sentences.text: Ayah saya menggunakan teknik pertanian yang baru.
sentences.en: My father uses new agricultural engineering methods.

note: 'Buat' is the informal spoken equivalent of 'untuk' (for); very common in casual speech but avoid in formal writing.

sentences.text: Ini kopi buat kamu.
sentences.en: This coffee is for you.

sentences.text: Saya beli oleh-oleh buat ibu.
sentences.en: I bought a souvenir for mom.

sentences.text: Nasi ini buat siapa?
sentences.en: Who is this rice for?

note: 'Bermasalah' means 'to have a problem' or 'problematic'; it is an adjective/verb formed with the prefix 'ber-' added to 'masalah' (problem); commonly used to describe people, things, or situations that are troublesome.

sentences.text: Motor saya bermasalah hari ini.
sentences.en: My motorbike has a problem today.

sentences.text: Wifi di sini sering bermasalah.
sentences.en: The wifi here often has problems.

sentences.text: Anak itu tidak bermasalah di sekolah.
sentences.en: That child does not have problems at school.

note: 'Gampang' means 'easy' in informal/colloquial Indonesian; 'mudah' is the more formal equivalent — both are widely used.

sentences.text: Soal ini gampang sekali untuk saya.
sentences.en: This question is very easy for me.

sentences.text: Masak nasi goreng itu gampang banget.
sentences.en: Cooking fried rice is really easy.

sentences.text: Bahasa Indonesia gampang dipelajari setiap hari.
sentences.en: Indonesian is easy to learn every day.

note: 'Kasus' is a neutral formal/informal word for 'case' (legal, medical, or general); commonly heard in news and everyday talk; related: 'masalah' (problem), 'perkara' (matter/case).

sentences.text: Kasus itu sudah selesai kemarin.
sentences.en: That case was already resolved yesterday.

sentences.text: Ada kasus baru di rumah sakit.
sentences.en: There is a new case at the hospital.

sentences.text: Polisi sedang menyelidiki kasus ini.
sentences.en: The police are investigating this case.

note: "Mikir" is the informal/colloquial form of "pikir" (to think); use "pikir" in formal writing, but "mikir" is very common in everyday spoken Indonesian.

sentences.text: Aku mikir mau makan apa hari ini.
sentences.en: I'm thinking about what to eat today.

sentences.text: Dia mikir sebentar sebelum menjawab.
sentences.en: He thought for a moment before answering.

sentences.text: Jangan mikir terlalu banyak, santai saja.
sentences.en: Don't think too much, just relax.

note: 'Milih' is the informal/colloquial form of 'pilih' (to choose); use 'pilih' in formal writing or speech.

sentences.text: Kamu mau milih makanan apa hari ini?
sentences.en: What food do you want to choose today?

sentences.text: Dia milih baju biru di toko itu.
sentences.en: She chose a blue shirt at that store.

sentences.text: Ayo milih satu oleh-oleh untuk ibu.
sentences.en: Come on, choose one souvenir for mom.

english: to chat, to talk about something (informal)
note: Informal verb for casual conversation; more relaxed than 'berbicara'; often used with 'sama' (with) or 'tentang' (about).

sentences.text: Kami ngobrol di warung tadi pagi.
sentences.en: We were chatting at the food stall this morning.

sentences.text: Dia suka ngobrol sama teman-temannya.
sentences.en: She likes to chat with her friends.

sentences.text: Ayo ngobrol sebentar di sini.
sentences.en: Let's chat for a moment here.

note: 'Nolong' is the informal/colloquial form of 'tolong'; 'tolong' also means 'please' when asking for help.

sentences.text: Bisa nolong saya bawa tas ini?
sentences.en: Can you help me carry this bag?

sentences.text: Dia nolong ibu di dapur tadi.
sentences.en: She helped mom in the kitchen earlier.

sentences.text: Tolong nolong teman kamu ya!
sentences.en: Please help your friend, okay!

note: 'Pengacara' means lawyer; note that 'acara' alone means 'event/program', so context matters.

sentences.text: Ayah saya adalah seorang pengacara terkenal.
sentences.en: My father is a famous lawyer.

sentences.text: Dia butuh pengacara untuk masalah itu.
sentences.en: He needs a lawyer for that problem.

note: 'Soal' informally means 'about/regarding'; often used in casual speech instead of 'tentang', common in everyday conversation.

sentences.text: Dia bertanya soal harga kamar itu.
sentences.en: He asked about the price of that room.

sentences.text: Kita bicara soal rencana besok ya.
sentences.en: Let's talk about tomorrow's plan.

sentences.text: Ibu tahu soal masalah itu.
sentences.en: Mom knows about that problem.

note: 'Soalnya' is casual/informal, used to explain a reason; similar to 'karena' but more conversational, common in spoken Indonesian.

sentences.text: Aku tidak mau makan, soalnya kenyang.
sentences.en: I don't want to eat, because I'm full.

sentences.text: Dia tidak datang, soalnya hujan deras.
sentences.en: She didn't come, the thing is it was raining heavily.

sentences.text: Kami pulang cepat, soalnya sudah malam.
sentences.en: We went home early, because it was already night.

note: "Studi pembangunan" is an academic/formal term for the university major or field of development studies; often seen in university contexts.

sentences.text: Dia kuliah jurusan studi pembangunan di universitas.
sentences.en: She studies development studies at university.

sentences.text: Studi pembangunan adalah jurusan yang menarik.
sentences.en: Development studies is an interesting major.

sentences.text: Kakak saya memilih studi pembangunan tahun ini.
sentences.en: My older sibling chose development studies this year.

note: "Teknik elektro" is the standard academic term for the electrical engineering field/major; often shortened to "teknik" in casual speech, not to be confused with "elektronik" (electronics as a consumer category).

sentences.text: Kakak saya kuliah di teknik elektro.
sentences.en: My older sibling studies electrical engineering.

sentences.text: Teknik elektro adalah jurusan yang populer.
sentences.en: Electrical engineering is a popular major.

sentences.text: Dia ingin masuk teknik elektro tahun ini.
sentences.en: He wants to enter electrical engineering this year.

note: "Terus" as a discourse connector means "and then" in informal speech; don't confuse with terus meaning "continue" or "straight ahead".

sentences.text: Saya makan, terus pergi ke pasar.
sentences.en: I ate, and then went to the market.

sentences.text: Dia mandi, terus tidur siang.
sentences.en: She showered, and then took a nap.

sentences.text: Kami main, terus pulang ke rumah.
sentences.en: We played, and then went home.

note: 'Bangsawan' means a noble or aristocrat; used in formal or historical contexts; related words: 'kebangsawanan' (nobility), not to be confused with 'bangsa' (nation/ethnic group).

sentences.text: Dia adalah seorang bangsawan dari Bali.
sentences.en: He is a noble from Bali.

sentences.text: Keluarga bangsawan itu sangat terkenal.
sentences.en: That noble family is very famous.

sentences.text: Istana itu milik seorang bangsawan tua.
sentences.en: That palace belongs to an old noble.

note: "Belum pernah" means "have never (done something yet)"; "belum" alone means "not yet", while "pernah" alone means "ever"; together they express that something has not happened up to now.

sentences.text: Saya belum pernah makan nasi goreng.
sentences.en: I have never eaten fried rice.

sentences.text: Dia belum pernah pergi ke Bali.
sentences.en: She has never gone to Bali.

sentences.text: Kami belum pernah naik motor bersama.
sentences.en: We have never ridden a motorbike together.

note: 'Bintang' means 'star' (in the sky); it also refers to the popular Indonesian beer brand and is used for celebrity/famous person ('artis bintang').

sentences.text: Langit malam penuh dengan bintang yang indah.
sentences.en: The night sky is full of beautiful stars.

sentences.text: Saya suka melihat bintang di pantai.
sentences.en: I like watching stars at the beach.

note: 'Penari' means dancer; formed from 'tari' (dance) + prefix 'pe-'; related: 'menari' (to dance), 'tarian' (a dance style).

sentences.text: Dia adalah penari Bali yang terkenal.
sentences.en: She is a famous Balinese dancer.

sentences.text: Para penari itu memakai baju merah.
sentences.en: The dancers are wearing red clothes.

sentences.text: Adik saya ingin jadi penari.
sentences.en: My younger sibling wants to become a dancer.

note: "Perdana menteri" means prime minister; Indonesia has a president ("presiden"), not a prime minister, so this term is used when discussing other countries.

sentences.text: Perdana menteri Inggris berbicara di televisi.
sentences.en: The prime minister of England is speaking on television.

sentences.text: Siapa perdana menteri Jepang sekarang?
sentences.en: Who is the prime minister of Japan now?

sentences.text: Saya baca berita tentang perdana menteri.
sentences.en: I read news about the prime minister.

note: 'Sampai sekarang' means 'until now / so far'; used in everyday speech to describe something continuing up to the present moment.

sentences.text: Sampai sekarang saya belum makan nasi.
sentences.en: So far I haven't eaten rice yet.

sentences.text: Dia sampai sekarang masih belajar bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: She is still learning Indonesian so far.

sentences.text: Sampai sekarang cuaca di Bali panas.
sentences.en: So far the weather in Bali is hot.

note: 'Sudah pernah' means 'have/has ever (done something)'; 'sudah' adds a sense of completion to 'pernah' (ever/once); often confused with 'pernah' alone, which is slightly less emphatic.

sentences.text: Saya sudah pernah makan nasi goreng.
sentences.en: I have eaten nasi goreng before.

sentences.text: Dia sudah pernah pergi ke Bali.
sentences.en: She has been to Bali before.

sentences.text: Kamu sudah pernah naik motor?
sentences.en: Have you ever ridden a motorbike?

note: "Belum biasa" means 'not yet accustomed to'; "belum" (not yet) differs from "tidak" (not), and "biasa" alone means 'usual/accustomed'.

sentences.text: Saya belum biasa makan nasi setiap hari.
sentences.en: I am not yet used to eating rice every day.

sentences.text: Dia belum biasa naik motor di Bali.
sentences.en: He is not yet used to riding a motorbike in Bali.

sentences.text: Kami belum biasa dengan cuaca panas ini.
sentences.en: We are not yet used to this hot weather.

note: "Berani" means brave/daring; often confused with "mau" (want to); related: "keberanian" (courage), "penakut" (coward)

sentences.text: Dia berani naik ke atas pohon.
sentences.en: He dares to climb up the tree.

sentences.text: Aku tidak berani makan durian.
sentences.en: I don't dare to eat durian.

sentences.text: Adik berani pergi ke sekolah sendiri.
sentences.en: My little sibling dares to go to school alone.

english: to be successful, to have success, to succeed
note: 'Berhasil' is a common everyday verb meaning to succeed or manage to do something; often confused with 'sukses' which is more formal/career-focused; related word: 'keberhasilan' (success/achievement).

sentences.text: Dia berhasil lulus ujian kemarin.
