sentences.en: She succeeded in passing the exam yesterday.

sentences.text: Saya berhasil membuat nasi goreng hari ini.
sentences.en: I succeeded in making fried rice today.

sentences.text: Anak itu berhasil naik sepeda sendiri.
sentences.en: That child managed to ride a bicycle by himself.

english: to be a speaker of a language
note: 'Berbahasa' means to speak/use a language; often confused with 'bicara' (to talk); related: 'bahasa' (language), 'berbicara' (to speak)

sentences.text: Dia berbahasa Inggris dengan sangat baik.
sentences.en: She speaks English very well.

sentences.text: Saya ingin berbahasa Indonesia setiap hari.
sentences.en: I want to speak Indonesian every day.

sentences.text: Orang Bali berbahasa Bali di rumah.
sentences.en: Balinese people speak Balinese at home.

note: 'Kayu jati' means teak wood, a prestigious hardwood in Indonesia; often used in furniture contexts; 'kayu' alone means wood/timber, so 'kayu jati' literally means 'teak wood'.

sentences.text: Meja ini dibuat dari kayu jati.
sentences.en: This table is made from teak wood.

sentences.text: Kayu jati sangat kuat dan mahal.
sentences.en: Teak wood is very strong and expensive.

sentences.text: Ayah membeli kursi kayu jati baru.
sentences.en: Dad bought a new teak wood chair.

note: 'Minuman keras' literally means 'hard drink'; often shortened to 'miras' in casual speech; the opposite is 'minuman ringan' (soft drink).

sentences.text: Toko itu tidak menjual minuman keras.
sentences.en: That shop does not sell alcoholic drinks.

sentences.text: Dia tidak suka minuman keras sama sekali.
sentences.en: He does not like alcoholic drinks at all.

note: 'Pedagang' means a seller/merchant/dealer; commonly used in markets; related words: 'berdagang' (to trade), 'perdagangan' (trade/commerce).

sentences.text: Pedagang itu menjual buah di pasar.
sentences.en: That merchant sells fruit at the market.

sentences.text: Ibu membeli sayur dari pedagang sayuran.
sentences.en: Mother buys vegetables from the vegetable seller.

sentences.text: Pedagang kaki lima ada di sini.
sentences.en: There is a street vendor here.

note: 'Pekerja' means 'a worker/employee'; related words are 'kerja' (work) and 'bekerja' (to work); used in both formal and informal contexts.

sentences.text: Dia adalah pekerja di hotel itu.
sentences.en: He/She is a worker at that hotel.

sentences.text: Pekerja itu datang pagi setiap hari.
sentences.en: That worker comes early every day.

sentences.text: Bapak saya seorang pekerja keras.
sentences.en: My father is a hard worker.

note: 'Pelatih' means coach or trainer; related words: 'melatih' (to train), 'latihan' (practice/exercise); not to be confused with 'guru' (teacher in a school).

sentences.text: Pelatih saya sangat baik dan sabar.
sentences.en: My coach is very good and patient.

sentences.text: Dia adalah pelatih sepak bola terkenal.
sentences.en: He is a famous football coach.

sentences.text: Pelatih kami berlatih setiap hari.
sentences.en: Our coach trains every day.

note: 'Pemimpin' (noun) means 'a leader/leader'; from root 'pimpin' (to lead); often confused with 'ketua' (chairperson/head of group).

sentences.text: Dia adalah pemimpin yang baik di sekolah.
sentences.en: He is a good leader at school.

sentences.text: Pemimpin desa itu sangat bijaksana.
sentences.en: The village leader is very wise.

note: 'Pengajar' means teacher/instructor (from root 'ajar' = to teach); more formal than 'guru', often used for instructors outside schools.

sentences.text: Pengajar saya sangat sabar dan baik.
sentences.en: My teacher is very patient and kind.

sentences.text: Dia adalah pengajar bahasa Inggris.
sentences.en: He is an English teacher.

sentences.text: Pengajar itu mengajar di kelas besar.
sentences.en: That teacher teaches in a big classroom.

note: 'Pengalaman' means experience (knowledge/skill gained over time); related: 'berpengalaman' (experienced/adjective), not to be confused with 'kejadian' (an event/incident).

sentences.text: Dia punya banyak pengalaman di dapur.
sentences.en: She has a lot of experience in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Ini pengalaman pertama saya naik motor.
sentences.en: This is my first experience riding a motorbike.

sentences.text: Pengalaman itu sangat menyenangkan bagi saya.
sentences.en: That experience was very enjoyable for me.

note: 'Pengelola' means manager or operator (of a place/business); from root 'kelola' (to manage); similar to 'manajer' but more formal/local.

sentences.text: Pengelola hotel itu sangat ramah.
sentences.en: The hotel manager is very friendly.

sentences.text: Saya berbicara dengan pengelola restoran ini.
sentences.en: I spoke with the manager of this restaurant.

sentences.text: Pengelola vila membantu tamu setiap hari.
sentences.en: The villa manager helps guests every day.

note: 'Penjual' means 'seller/vendor'; the root verb 'jual' means 'to sell'; related: 'pembeli' (buyer), 'menjual' (to sell).

sentences.text: Penjual itu menjual buah di pasar.
sentences.en: That seller sells fruit at the market.

sentences.text: Saya membeli nasi dari penjual ini.
sentences.en: I buy rice from this seller.

sentences.text: Penjual itu ramah dan murah.
sentences.en: That seller is friendly and cheap.

note: 'Penulis' means writer/author; root verb is 'tulis' (to write); related: 'tulisan' (writing/text), 'menulis' (to write).

sentences.text: Dia adalah penulis buku terkenal.
sentences.en: She is a famous book author.

sentences.text: Ayah saya seorang penulis.
sentences.en: My father is a writer.

sentences.text: Penulis itu tinggal di Bali.
sentences.en: That writer lives in Bali.

note: 'Penyanyi' means 'singer'; formed from 'nyanyi' (to sing) + prefix 'pe-'; use 'penyanyi terkenal' for 'famous singer'.

sentences.text: Dia adalah penyanyi yang sangat terkenal.
sentences.en: She is a very famous singer.

sentences.text: Saya ingin menjadi penyanyi profesional.
sentences.en: I want to become a professional singer.

sentences.text: Penyanyi itu tampil di panggung besar.
sentences.en: The singer performed on a big stage.

note: 'Petugas' means an official worker or staffer (e.g. security guard, officer); more formal than 'karyawan' (employee).

sentences.text: Petugas itu membantu saya di bandara.
sentences.en: The staffer helped me at the airport.

sentences.text: Ada petugas di depan hotel.
sentences.en: There is a staffer in front of the hotel.

sentences.text: Saya bertanya kepada petugas keamanan.
sentences.en: I asked the security staffer.

note: 'Rokok' means cigarette; very common word in Indonesia, also seen in 'merokok' (to smoke); informal everyday register.

sentences.text: Dia membeli rokok di warung dekat rumah.
sentences.en: He buys a cigarette at the small shop near home.

sentences.text: Dilarang merokok di sini.
sentences.en: Smoking is not allowed here.

sentences.text: Ayah tidak mau merokok lagi sekarang.
sentences.en: Dad does not want to smoke anymore now.

note: "Sudah biasa" means 'already used to / accustomed to'; more casual than "terbiasa", very common in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Saya sudah biasa makan nasi setiap hari.
sentences.en: I am used to eating rice every day.

sentences.text: Dia sudah biasa bangun pagi.
sentences.en: She is used to waking up early.

sentences.text: Kami sudah biasa dengan cuaca panas.
sentences.en: We are used to the hot weather.

note: 'Traktor' is a direct loanword from Dutch/English; used in farming contexts, often seen in rural Bali and Java.

sentences.text: Petani itu menggunakan traktor di sawah.
sentences.en: That farmer uses a tractor in the rice field.

sentences.text: Traktor besar itu milik pak Wayan.
sentences.en: That big tractor belongs to Mr. Wayan.

sentences.text: Ayah membeli traktor baru kemarin.
sentences.en: Father bought a new tractor yesterday.

note: 'Angka' means number/digit/figure; don't confuse with 'nomor' (a specific assigned number, e.g. phone number or address); related: 'angka satu' (number one), 'angka besar' (large number).

sentences.text: Angka tujuh adalah angka kesukaanku.
sentences.en: Seven is my favorite number.

sentences.text: Tulis angka satu sampai sepuluh.
sentences.en: Write the numbers one to ten.

sentences.text: Angka di harga itu sangat besar.
sentences.en: The figure on that price is very large.

note: 'Bercerita' means to tell a story or narrate; related to 'cerita' (story), more expressive than 'bilang' (to say/tell).

sentences.text: Ibu bercerita tentang masa kecilnya.
sentences.en: Mom tells a story about her childhood.

sentences.text: Andi bercerita kepada teman-temannya.
sentences.en: Andi tells a story to his friends.

sentences.text: Saya suka bercerita sebelum tidur.
sentences.en: I like to tell stories before sleeping.

note: 'Berpengalaman' means experienced/skilled; formed by prefix 'ber-' + 'pengalaman' (experience); commonly used in job contexts; related: 'pengalaman' (experience), 'ahli' (expert).

sentences.text: Dokter itu sangat berpengalaman dan baik.
sentences.en: That doctor is very experienced and kind.

sentences.text: Saya mencari guru yang berpengalaman.
sentences.en: I am looking for an experienced teacher.

sentences.text: Sopir ini berpengalaman di Bali.
sentences.en: This driver is experienced in Bali.

note: 'Bersedia' means 'to be willing/ready'; more formal than 'mau'; often used in polite requests or offers.

sentences.text: Apakah kamu bersedia membantu saya?
sentences.en: Are you willing to help me?

sentences.text: Saya bersedia belajar bahasa Indonesia.
sentences.en: I am willing to learn Indonesian.

sentences.text: Dia bersedia pergi ke pasar.
sentences.en: She is willing to go to the market.

note: 'Cewek' is informal/colloquial for a girl or young woman; use 'perempuan' or 'wanita' in formal contexts.

sentences.text: Cewek itu sangat cantik dan ramah.
sentences.en: That girl is very pretty and friendly.

sentences.text: Siapa nama cewek di sana?
sentences.en: What is the name of that girl over there?

sentences.text: Dia cewek yang suka surfing.
sentences.en: She is a girl who likes surfing.

note: "Dua kali" means "twice" or "two times"; use it before a verb or noun to show frequency, similar to "sekali" (once) and "tiga kali" (three times).

sentences.text: Saya makan dua kali sehari.
sentences.en: I eat twice a day.

sentences.text: Dia sudah pergi dua kali ke Bali.
sentences.en: She has gone to Bali twice.

sentences.text: Kami latihan dua kali seminggu.
sentences.en: We practice twice a week.

note: 'Ganti' means to replace or change something; commonly used for changing clothes ('ganti baju') or replacing items; related words: 'mengganti' (formal), 'pertukaran' (exchange).

sentences.text: Saya perlu ganti baju sekarang.
sentences.en: I need to change clothes now.

sentences.text: Tolong ganti air minum ini.
sentences.en: Please replace this drinking water.

sentences.text: Dia ganti sepatu di rumah.
sentences.en: She changes shoes at home.

note: 'Kartu' is a neutral everyday word for any card (ID card, playing card, credit card); common phrases include 'kartu identitas' (ID card) and 'kartu kredit' (credit card).

sentences.text: Saya punya kartu identitas baru.
sentences.en: I have a new identity card.

sentences.text: Dia membayar dengan kartu kredit.
sentences.en: She pays with a credit card.

sentences.text: Tolong tunjukkan kartu Anda kepada saya.
sentences.en: Please show me your card.

note: 'Komponen' is a neutral, everyday loanword used in technical and general contexts; often heard in electronics, cooking, and education.

sentences.text: Komponen mesin ini sudah rusak.
sentences.en: This machine's component is already broken.

sentences.text: Ada satu komponen yang hilang.
sentences.en: There is one component that is missing.

sentences.text: Kita perlu membeli komponen baru.
sentences.en: We need to buy a new component.

note: 'Surat lamaran' specifically means a written job application letter; often confused with 'lamaran' alone which can also mean a marriage proposal.

sentences.text: Dia menulis surat lamaran untuk pekerjaan baru.
sentences.en: He writes an application letter for a new job.

sentences.text: Saya sudah kirim surat lamaran ke kantor.
sentences.en: I have already sent an application letter to the office.

sentences.text: Surat lamaran itu sangat bagus.
sentences.en: That application letter is very good.

english: to fit, instal, set/put something in a place
note: "Memasang" is the active verb form of "pasang"; used for installing, fitting, or placing things like lights, tires, or signs — often confused with "meletakkan" (to place/put down gently).

sentences.text: Ayah memasang lampu baru di kamar.
sentences.en: Dad is installing a new light in the room.

sentences.text: Dia memasang ban sepeda dengan cepat.
sentences.en: He fits the bicycle tire quickly.

sentences.text: Ibu memasang foto di dinding rumah.
sentences.en: Mom puts a photo on the house wall.

note: 'Ngomong' is informal/colloquial for 'to talk or say'; use 'berbicara' or 'berkata' in formal writing; commonly heard in everyday conversation across Indonesia.

sentences.text: Dia ngomong pelan sekali di kelas.
sentences.en: She speaks very softly in class.

sentences.text: Kamu ngomong apa tadi?
sentences.en: What did you say just now?

sentences.text: Kami ngomong tentang liburan ke Bali.
sentences.en: We talked about a holiday to Bali.

note: 'Nyanyi' is the informal/colloquial form of 'bernyanyi' (to sing); commonly used in everyday speech; related words: 'lagu' (song), 'penyanyi' (singer).

sentences.text: Dia suka nyanyi di kamar mandi.
sentences.en: She likes to sing in the bathroom.

sentences.text: Kami nyanyi lagu bersama di pantai.
sentences.en: We sing songs together at the beach.

sentences.text: Adik nyanyi dengan suara yang merdu.
sentences.en: My younger sibling sings with a beautiful voice.

note: 'Paling tidak' means 'at least' and is common in everyday speech; similar to 'setidaknya', it sets a minimum expectation.

sentences.text: Minum paling tidak dua gelas air sehari.
sentences.en: Drink at least two glasses of water a day.

sentences.text: Dia belajar paling tidak satu jam.
sentences.en: He studies for at least one hour.

sentences.text: Kita perlu paling tidak lima orang.
sentences.en: We need at least five people.

note: 'Resepsionis' is a loanword from English, used in hotels and offices; neutral register, also related to 'resepsi' (reception event).

sentences.text: Resepsionis itu sangat ramah dan sopan.
sentences.en: The receptionist is very friendly and polite.

sentences.text: Saya bertanya kepada resepsionis di hotel.
sentences.en: I asked the receptionist at the hotel.

sentences.text: Resepsionis memberikan kunci kamar kepada saya.
sentences.en: The receptionist gave me the room key.

note: 'Riwayat hidup' means biography or life history; often used in formal/job contexts; also called 'biografi' for a written biography book.

sentences.text: Saya menulis riwayat hidup saya sendiri.
sentences.en: I write my own biography.

sentences.text: Dia membaca riwayat hidup pahlawan itu.
sentences.en: He reads the biography of that hero.

sentences.text: Riwayat hidup Pak Budi sangat menarik.
sentences.en: Mr. Budi's biography is very interesting.

note: 'Asal' meaning 'on condition that/as long as' can be confused with 'asal' meaning 'origin'; in conditional use it connects a condition to a result.

sentences.text: Kamu boleh pergi asal sudah makan.
sentences.en: You may go on condition that you have eaten.

sentences.text: Dia mau membantu asal ada waktu.
sentences.en: She is willing to help as long as she has time.

sentences.text: Anak itu boleh main asal rajin belajar.
sentences.en: That child may play on condition that he studies hard.

note: 'Hormat' means respect or honor; used in greetings like 'hormat saya' (my regards) and the verb 'menghormati' (to respect someone).

sentences.text: Kita harus hormat kepada orang tua.
sentences.en: We must respect our parents.

sentences.text: Dia memberi hormat kepada gurunya.
sentences.en: He shows respect to his teacher.

sentences.text: Hormat adalah nilai yang sangat penting.
sentences.en: Respect is a very important value.

note: 'Iklan' means advertisement or commercial; used for TV ads, online ads, and posters; related word 'mengiklankan' means to advertise something.

sentences.text: Saya melihat iklan di televisi tadi.
sentences.en: I saw an advertisement on television just now.

sentences.text: Iklan ini sangat menarik dan lucu.
sentences.en: This advertisement is very interesting and funny.

sentences.text: Dia memasang iklan di internet kemarin.
sentences.en: She posted an advertisement on the internet yesterday.

note: "Kepala kantor" literally means "head of office" and is a formal title; similar terms include "kepala sekolah" (school principal) and "kepala desa" (village head).

sentences.text: Kepala kantor itu sangat baik dan ramah.
sentences.en: The office head is very kind and friendly.

sentences.text: Saya ingin bertemu dengan kepala kantor.
sentences.en: I want to meet the office head.

sentences.text: Kepala kantor sedang rapat sekarang.
sentences.en: The office head is in a meeting now.

note: 'Lupa' means 'to forget'; used for both 'I forget' and 'I forgot'; related word: 'melupakan' (to forget something intentionally or over time).

sentences.text: Saya lupa membawa dompet hari ini.
sentences.en: I forgot to bring my wallet today.

sentences.text: Dia lupa nama teman barunya.
sentences.en: She forgot her new friend's name.

sentences.text: Jangan lupa minum air setiap hari.
sentences.en: Don't forget to drink water every day.

note: 'Melalui' means 'through' or 'by way of'; used for routes or methods; more formal than 'lewat' but both are common

sentences.text: Kami pergi melalui jalan kecil itu.
sentences.en: We go through that small road.

sentences.text: Dia belajar bahasa Inggris melalui internet.
sentences.en: She learns English through the internet.

sentences.text: Pesan dikirim melalui email kemarin.
sentences.en: The message was sent by email yesterday.

english: to apply for (a job), to formally ask for a woman's hand in marriage
note: "Melamar" means both applying for a job and formally proposing marriage; context makes the meaning clear; related words: lamaran (application/proposal), pelamar (applicant).

sentences.text: Dia melamar kerja di restoran itu.
sentences.en: He applied for a job at that restaurant.

sentences.text: Budi melamar kekasihnya minggu lalu.
sentences.en: Budi proposed to his girlfriend last week.

note: 'Mengendarai' is the formal/written form; in casual speech Indonesians often say 'naik' (ride/take) for motorbikes, but 'mengendarai' covers both cars and motorbikes.

sentences.text: Saya mengendarai motor ke pasar.
sentences.en: I ride a motorbike to the market.

sentences.text: Ayah mengendarai mobil ke kantor.
sentences.en: Father drives a car to the office.

sentences.text: Dia belajar mengendarai sepeda hari ini.
sentences.en: She is learning to ride a bicycle today.

note: 'Perhatian' means attention or notice; used in announcements ('perhatian!') and to mean care/concern; related: 'memperhatikan' (to pay attention to).

sentences.text: Perhatian! Bus akan segera berangkat.
sentences.en: Attention! The bus will depart soon.

sentences.text: Guru meminta perhatian dari semua siswa.
sentences.en: The teacher asked for attention from all students.

sentences.text: Tolong beri perhatian kepada adikmu.
sentences.en: Please give attention to your younger sibling.

note: 'Terserah' means 'up to you / whatever you like'; very common in casual speech; can sound dismissive if said with a flat tone; related: 'bebas' (free choice), 'pilih saja' (just choose).

sentences.text: Mau makan apa? Terserah kamu saja.
sentences.en: What do you want to eat? It's up to you.

sentences.text: Terserah, kita bisa pergi ke pantai.
sentences.en: Up to you, we can go to the beach.

sentences.text: Pilih bajunya terserah kamu ya.
sentences.en: Choose the clothes, it's up to you.

note: 'Wawancara' means interview (job or media); formal register, not used for casual chats; related: 'pewawancara' (interviewer), 'diwawancarai' (to be interviewed).

sentences.text: Besok saya ada wawancara kerja pagi.
sentences.en: Tomorrow I have a job interview in the morning.

sentences.text: Dia gugup sebelum wawancara itu.
sentences.en: She was nervous before the interview.

sentences.text: Wawancara saya berlangsung satu jam.
sentences.en: My interview lasted one hour.

note: 'Bidan' means midwife; commonly confused with 'dokter' (doctor) — a bidan specialises in pregnancy and childbirth, not general medicine.

sentences.text: Ibu pergi ke bidan setiap bulan.
sentences.en: Mother goes to the midwife every month.

sentences.text: Bidan itu sangat baik dan sabar.
sentences.en: The midwife is very kind and patient.

sentences.text: Adik lahir dibantu oleh bidan.
sentences.en: My younger sibling was born with help from a midwife.

note: 'Cucu' means grandchild (grandson or granddaughter); it is gender-neutral, related words include 'kakek' (grandfather) and 'nenek' (grandmother).

sentences.text: Nenek sangat menyayangi cucu perempuannya.
sentences.en: Grandma loves her granddaughter very much.

sentences.text: Cucu kakek bermain di taman.
sentences.en: Grandfather's grandchild plays in the park.

sentences.text: Saya punya satu cucu laki-laki.
sentences.en: I have one grandson.

note: "Dibandingkan" means "compared to" and is often used to contrast two things; commonly confused with "membandingkan" (to compare actively); related: "sama" (same), "lebih" (more).

sentences.text: Apel ini lebih manis dibandingkan jeruk itu.
sentences.en: This apple is sweeter compared to that orange.

sentences.text: Bali lebih panas dibandingkan Jakarta.
sentences.en: Bali is hotter compared to Jakarta.

sentences.text: Motor ini lebih murah dibandingkan mobil.
sentences.en: This motorbike is cheaper compared to a car.

note: "Dokter hewan" literally means 'animal doctor'; use it for vets treating pets or farm animals — do not shorten to just "dokter" as that refers to a human doctor.

sentences.text: Anjing saya sakit, perlu ke dokter hewan.
sentences.en: My dog is sick, needs to go to the vet.

sentences.text: Dokter hewan itu baik sekali.
sentences.en: That vet is very kind.

sentences.text: Ibu membawa kucing ke dokter hewan.
sentences.en: Mom is taking the cat to the vet.

note: 'Film horor' is casual everyday Indonesian for a horror movie; 'film' can also mean 'movie' generally, and 'horor' is borrowed from English.

sentences.text: Saya tidak suka nonton film horor.
sentences.en: I don't like watching a horror movie.

sentences.text: Adik saya takut film horor.
sentences.en: My younger sibling is scared of horror movies.

sentences.text: Malam ini kita nonton film horor.
sentences.en: Tonight we are watching a horror movie.

note: "Hobi" is an informal loanword from English; used in casual speech and writing, interchangeable with "kegemaran" in formal contexts.

sentences.text: Hobi saya adalah memasak dan membaca.
sentences.en: My hobby is cooking and reading.

sentences.text: Apa hobi kamu sehari-hari?
sentences.en: What is your everyday hobby?

sentences.text: Dia punya hobi bermain gitar.
sentences.en: He has a hobby of playing guitar.

note: "Ijazah" is a formal/neutral word for a school or university diploma; often needed for job applications; related: "gelar" (degree title), "sertifikat" (certificate).

sentences.text: Saya sudah mendapat ijazah dari universitas.
sentences.en: I have already received a diploma from the university.

sentences.text: Ijazah saya ada di rumah.
sentences.en: My diploma is at home.

sentences.text: Dia butuh ijazah untuk melamar kerja.
sentences.en: She needs a diploma to apply for a job.

note: "Kaca mata" (also spelled "kacamata") means eyeglasses; not to be confused with "kaca" (glass/mirror) alone; related: "kaca mata hitam" (sunglasses).

sentences.text: Saya pakai kaca mata setiap hari.
sentences.en: I wear glasses every day.

sentences.text: Di mana kaca mata saya?
sentences.en: Where are my glasses?

sentences.text: Ibu membeli kaca mata baru kemarin.
sentences.en: Mom bought new glasses yesterday.

note: 'Kekurangan' means 'to lack' or 'to be short of'; it combines 'kurang' (not enough) with the prefix/suffix ke-an; often confused with 'tidak ada' (there is none at all).

sentences.text: Kami kekurangan beras di dapur.
sentences.en: We are short of rice in the kitchen.

sentences.text: Toko itu kekurangan air minum.
sentences.en: That shop is short of drinking water.

sentences.text: Saya kekurangan uang untuk makan.
sentences.en: I am short of money to eat.

note: 'Kuda' means horse; related words include 'kuda-kuda' (a stance/tripod) and 'berkuda' (to ride a horse); neutral everyday register.

sentences.text: Anak itu melihat kuda di ladang.
sentences.en: That child sees a horse in the field.

sentences.text: Kuda itu berlari sangat cepat.
sentences.en: The horse runs very fast.

sentences.text: Saya ingin naik kuda besok.
sentences.en: I want to ride a horse tomorrow.

note: 'Mata' means 'eye'; also appears in compounds like 'kacamata' (glasses) and 'mata uang' (currency); register is neutral/everyday.

sentences.text: Mata saya sakit hari ini.
sentences.en: My eye hurts today.

sentences.text: Dia menutup mata karena lelah.
sentences.en: She closes her eyes because she is tired.

sentences.text: Anak itu punya mata biru.
sentences.en: That child has blue eyes.

english: to serve someone, to attend to (customers)
note: 'Melayani' means to serve or attend to someone, commonly used in shops, restaurants, and hotels; related to 'layanan' (service) and 'pelayan' (waiter/server).

sentences.text: Dia melayani tamu di hotel itu.
sentences.en: She serves the guests at that hotel.

sentences.text: Ibu melayani pembeli di toko kecil.
sentences.en: Mom attends to customers at the small shop.

sentences.text: Pelayan itu melayani kami dengan ramah.
sentences.en: That waiter served us in a friendly way.

note: 'Panitia' means a committee or organizing team; commonly used for events and school activities; related: 'ketua panitia' (committee head).

sentences.text: Panitia acara itu bekerja dengan keras.
sentences.en: The event committee works very hard.

sentences.text: Saya bergabung dengan panitia sekolah.
sentences.en: I joined the school committee.

sentences.text: Panitia sudah menyiapkan semua makanan.
sentences.en: The committee has prepared all the food.

note: 'Penyakit' means 'disease' or 'illness'; related words include 'sakit' (sick/pain) and 'obat' (medicine); used in both formal and everyday speech.

sentences.text: Dokter bilang dia punya penyakit serius.
sentences.en: The doctor said he has a serious disease.

sentences.text: Penyakit flu sangat mudah menular.
sentences.en: The flu disease spreads very easily.

sentences.text: Cuci tangan bisa mencegah penyakit.
sentences.en: Washing hands can prevent disease.

note: 'Praktis' means practical or convenient; often used to describe handy tools or easy solutions; related to 'praktik' (practice/clinic).

sentences.text: Tas ini sangat praktis untuk dibawa.
sentences.en: This bag is very practical to carry.

sentences.text: Cara ini lebih praktis dan mudah.
sentences.en: This way is more practical and easy.

sentences.text: Sepatu itu praktis untuk sehari-hari.
sentences.en: Those shoes are practical for everyday use.

note: 'Puskesmas' is an acronym for 'Pusat Kesehatan Masyarakat'; it refers to a government-run community health clinic found in every district across Indonesia, often the first point of care for locals.

sentences.text: Saya pergi ke Puskesmas hari ini.
sentences.en: I am going to the community health centre today.

sentences.text: Puskesmas ini dekat dengan rumah saya.
sentences.en: This community health centre is close to my house.

sentences.text: Dokter di Puskesmas sangat ramah.
sentences.en: The doctor at the community health centre is very friendly.

note: "Sakit jantung" literally means "heart sickness"; use "punya sakit jantung" (to have heart disease) or simply say someone "kena sakit jantung"; not to be confused with "serangan jantung" (heart attack).

sentences.text: Kakek saya punya sakit jantung sejak lama.
sentences.en: My grandfather has had heart disease for a long time.

sentences.text: Dokter bilang dia kena sakit jantung.
sentences.en: The doctor said he has heart disease.

sentences.text: Ibu tidak makan lemak karena sakit jantung.
sentences.en: Mom does not eat fat because of heart disease.

note: "Salon kecantikan" means beauty salon; "kecantikan" comes from "cantik" (beautiful/pretty); commonly shortened to just "salon" in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Ibu pergi ke salon kecantikan hari ini.
sentences.en: Mom goes to the beauty salon today.

sentences.text: Ada salon kecantikan dekat pasar.
sentences.en: There is a beauty salon near the market.

sentences.text: Saya potong rambut di salon kecantikan.
sentences.en: I cut my hair at the beauty salon.

note: "Sarjana muda" is a formal/academic term for a bachelor's degree holder; in everyday speech Indonesians often just say "S1" or "sarjana".

sentences.text: Kakak saya sudah lulus sarjana muda.
sentences.en: My older sibling has already graduated with a bachelor's degree.

sentences.text: Dia ingin mendapat gelar sarjana muda.
sentences.en: He wants to get a bachelor's degree.

note: "Seksi" means 'section' or 'department' in formal/organizational contexts; beginners may confuse it with the English loanword 'sexy' — they are spelled the same but context makes the meaning clear.

sentences.text: Saya bekerja di seksi keuangan.
sentences.en: I work in the finance section.

sentences.text: Seksi makanan ada di lantai dua.
sentences.en: The food section is on the second floor.

sentences.text: Tolong pergi ke seksi informasi.
sentences.en: Please go to the information section.

note: 'Skripsi' refers specifically to an undergraduate thesis in Indonesia; commonly discussed by university students; related words: 'tesis' (graduate thesis), 'sidang' (thesis defense).

sentences.text: Dia sedang menulis skripsi di perpustakaan.
sentences.en: She is writing a thesis in the library.

sentences.text: Skripsi saya tentang budaya Bali.
sentences.en: My thesis is about Balinese culture.

sentences.text: Kapan kamu selesai skripsi?
sentences.en: When will you finish your thesis?

note: 'Tebal' means thick (for objects like books, walls, or fabric); opposite is 'tipis' (thin); do not confuse with 'gemuk' (fat, for people).

sentences.text: Buku ini sangat tebal dan berat.
sentences.en: This book is very thick and heavy.

sentences.text: Dinding rumah itu tebal sekali.
sentences.en: That house's wall is very thick.

sentences.text: Saya pakai baju tebal karena dingin.
sentences.en: I wear a thick shirt because it is cold.

note: 'Tergantung pada' means 'to depend on'; often shortened to just 'tergantung' in casual speech; do not confuse with 'menggantung' (to hang something).

sentences.text: Harga tiket tergantung pada musim liburan.
sentences.en: The ticket price depends on the holiday season.

sentences.text: Rencana kami tergantung pada cuaca hari ini.
sentences.en: Our plan depends on today's weather.

sentences.text: Pilihan makanan tergantung pada selera kamu.
sentences.en: The food choice depends on your taste.

note: "Tergantung" means physically hanging/suspended, but is also very commonly used to mean "it depends" in everyday speech.

sentences.text: Tas itu tergantung di balik pintu.
sentences.en: That bag is hanging behind the door.

sentences.text: Handuk saya tergantung di kamar mandi.
sentences.en: My towel is hanging in the bathroom.
